note: Every quirk the skeptics kept (verdict verified or adjusted), with the exact supporting quote, sources and the skeptic's note. 0 were unsupported.

kept.description: Coat markings, not body shape. Thomas Darley's 1703 letter describes a bay with an unusually large blaze down the face ('something of the largest') and white on the near fore and both hind feet. Fits no build or gait parameter; could feed a face-marking option.
kept.quote: His colour is bay, and his near fore-foot before, with his hind-feet, has white upon them. He has a blaze down his face, something of the largest. He is about fifteen hands high
kept.note: I re-fetched the archived bloodlines.net bio. It quotes Thomas Darley's letter of 21 December 1703 about this horse word for word, and the quote is there exactly.

kept.description: High, arched, heavy crest. English Wikipedia (citing Whyte, 1840) calls it 'unnaturally high', and Berenger, who saw him, said 'his crest was high'. The very oversized crest appears mainly in the Stubbs versions of his portrait, which were criticised and disputed, so the value is set a bit below the extreme.
kept.quote: He stood at {{hands|15}} and was distinguished by an unnaturally high crest, which is noticeable from portraits of the horse. / He had a small head on a well arched and crested neck / His crest was high / the Stubbs versions are the only ones in which the horse is presented with the unattractive, and to some, overly large, crest which was also the subject of much criticism and controversy.
kept.note: All the quotes are there. But bloodlines.net says the 'overly large' crest appears only in the Stubbs portraits, which were probably copied from the Morier, and that this depiction was itself criticised and disputed. So the claim that 'critics called it overly large' was a misreading. I kept the trait, because Wikipedia says 'unnaturally high' and Berenger, who saw him, says 'crest was high'. I lowered the value from 1.5 to 1.4 so it does not copy the Stubbs exaggeration.

kept.description: Large ears. The vet Osmer noted the 'plainness of his head and ears', and the Morier portrait, the only one painted from life, shows large ears.
kept.quote: His plain head and large ears are well illustrated by Morier
kept.note: The quote is there word for word, along with Osmer's 'considering the plainness of his head and ears'. A value of 1.15 is fair for 'large ears'.

kept.description: Wide-set ears. Richard Berenger (Gentleman of the Horse to George III) described the roots of the ears as wide apart.
kept.quote: described him as plain-headed, with the roots of ears being wide apart
kept.note: The quote is there exactly, attributed to Richard Berenger, Gentleman of the Horse to King George III.

kept.description: Lop ears that droop noticeably outward. The source says his descendant Melbourne inherited them.
kept.quote: the ears themselves having a noticeable outward droop ... perhaps his lop ears are best presented in the Marshall portrait. It would seem that his descendant, Melbourne (br c 1834), twice a Champion Sire, came by his lop ears honestly.
kept.note: The quote is there exactly. A value of 0.6 is a moderate droop, which is fair for 'noticeable outward droop'.

kept.description: Very powerful, broad hindquarters with high, broad loins. The veterinarian Osmer, who knew the horse, said these were stronger than in any horse of his size.
kept.quote: the muscles of his loins rose exceedingly high, broad, and expanded, which were inserted into his hindquarters with greater strength and power than in any horse I believe ever yet seen of his dimensions / was short-backed with tremendous quarters and a high-set tail
kept.note: Both phrases are there exactly on tbheritage, and English Wikipedia carries the same Osmer passage. De Manty's 'his quarters broad in spite of being half starved' supports it too.

kept.description: High-set tail, carried in the Arabian style.
kept.quote: short-backed with tremendous quarters and a high-set tail / tail carried in true Arabian style
kept.note: Both phrases are on tbheritage. English Wikipedia also mentions portraits that show 'a high-carried tail'.

kept.description: Very short back behind deep shoulders that are well laid back. Fits no current parameter; candidate for back length or shoulder slope.
kept.quote: his shoulders were deeper, and lay farther into his back, than those of any horse ever yet seen. Behind the shoulders, there was but a very small space ere the muscles of his loins rose
kept.note: This is Osmer's description, word for word on tbheritage and nearly the same on English Wikipedia.

kept.description: Slightly over at the knees (knees sprung forward), with heavy shoulders. A foreleg-conformation trait; candidate parameter.
kept.quote: His crest was high, his shoulders heavy and he was slightly over at the knees.
kept.note: The quote is there exactly (Berenger). Osmer also mentions 'the position of his fore-legs' as a flaw.

kept.description: Very long, plain face. Takeda Bungo, Shinzan's trainer, who remembered him from that era, said his face was long, 'really horse-like' [顔は長くて、ホント、馬みたい]. His jockey Konishi Kizo (quoted in 『調教師の本』) called him 'the horse-faced horse of horse faces' [馬面中の馬面]. Mapped to a somewhat larger head.
kept.quote: 顔は長くて、ホント、馬みたい（笑い）。 / セントライトは馬面中の馬面で好男子ではなかったが、利口で丈夫。
kept.note: Both quotes are there. The second was wrongly credited to 'his own trainer'. It is Konishi Kizo, his jockey (the infobox lists Tanaka Waichiro as trainer), and Takeda was Shinzan's trainer, not his. Both quotes describe a long face, not a big head, so I lowered head size from 1.1 to 1.07 so it is not read as a 'very big head'.

kept.description: Big hooves. JRA board member Aoki Eiichi remembered the huge black horse plodding onto the track on big hooves 'like a bull in the dark' [大きな蹄で、ノッシノッシ].
kept.quote: 黒い巨体を、私の記憶では大きな蹄で、ノッシノッシという感じで馬場に出てくる様子は、暗闇の牛という感じであった
kept.note: The quote is there exactly (青木栄一, 日本中央競馬会理事, 『優駿』1977年2月号). It is one person's memory, but 1.08 is a fair reading.

kept.description: Large, stocky, unrefined build (166 cm at the withers, about 500 kg+, very big for his era). He was mocked as a 'squat, chunky heavy tank' [ずんぐりむっくりの大型戦車]. Mapped to a rounder barrel; overall size has no parameter.
kept.quote: 東京優駿出走時に計測された体高…は166cm、推定体重は500kg以上と、当時としては大型馬であったが、スマートさに欠ける体型で「ずんぐりむっくりの大型戦車」などと揶揄されていた
kept.note: The quote is there in the 身体面の特徴 section. A modest 1.06 is a fair proxy for 'stocky'.

kept.description: Upright (steep) shoulder [肩は立ってて]. Candidate shoulder-angle parameter.
kept.quote: 肩は立ってて、ドスン、ドスンて走り方をする。
kept.note: Takeda Bungo said it in 『競馬四季報 1978年冬号』. The quote is there exactly.

kept.description: Heavy, thudding, ponderous running action ('dosun, dosun') [ドスン、ドスンて走り方], unlike the light, quick Minami More. Candidate gait-weight or footfall-impact parameter.
kept.quote: これがまた鈍重な格好でね。…ドスン、ドスンて走り方をする。…モッサリ型のセントライトが勝つんだから。
kept.note: All the pieces are in the same Takeda quotation block.

kept.description: Long body and long legs, a typical stayer's build [胴長・脚長という典型的なステイヤーの体型]. Candidate body-length and leg-length parameters.
kept.quote: 胴長・脚長という典型的なステイヤーの体型を持ち、もっとも得意としたのも長距離競走であった。
kept.note: The quote is there exactly in the characteristics section.

kept.description: As a foal and yearling he was very long-legged, tall and slender with a shallow chest [胸の薄い細身]. This describes him only as a youngster. The documented adult build is just 'long body, long legs', so it should not set the adult chest depth.
kept.quote: 幼駒の頃は脚が非常に長く、背は高いが胸の薄い細身の馬で目立った存在ではなかった。
kept.note: The quote is there, but it is explicitly about 幼駒の頃 (as a foal or youngster), so chestDepth 0.95 was not a fair reading for the adult racehorse. I removed the parameter (now null) and kept the trait as a note only.

kept.description: Habit of raising his head and neck to look around [首をあげて周りを確かめるしぐさ]. Farm manager Matsushima Mitsuyoshi recorded it as Speed Symboli's habit, passed on to his grandson Symboli Rudolf. Not a racing head carriage.
kept.quote: 祖父のスピードシンボリの癖だった首をあげて周りを確かめるしぐさは、あの子に受けついでいます
kept.note: The quote is there exactly on the Symboli Rudolf page (松島光好, citing 今井寿恵 1985, p88).

kept.description: After the finish he habitually neighed loudly with tears running, as if complaining about being made to race. Post-race behaviour; candidate for an animation or behaviour parameter.
kept.quote: スピードシンボリはゴール後にレースを走らされた事への不平不満を訴えるように、涙を流しながら大声で鳴く習慣があり
kept.note: The quote is there exactly, per jockey Nohira (『優駿』2000年3月号 p.47).

kept.description: Ran with the neck lowered, pushing straight ahead [首を下げたまま走る / クビを少し下げて]. Jockey Masuzawa said this made him hard to ride.
kept.quote: また首を下げたまま走るハイセイコーとは騎乗時に人馬一体の感覚を味わえなかったとし / クビを少し下げてひたすら前に進もうとする走行フォーム
kept.note: Both quotes are there exactly. 'Slightly lowered' supports a moderate -0.45 rather than an extreme value.

kept.description: Very long stride: the press reported 8 m per stride [ひと跳び8メートル]. He looked slow because of the big stride but was fast.
kept.quote: ハイセイコーはストライドの大きな馬で、マスコミは「ひと跳び8メートル」と報じた
kept.note: The quote is there exactly. 8 m against the roughly 7.3 m average of the era is about 1.1.

kept.description: Very strong hind legs; he ran on power rather than smoothness and wore out his hind shoes in about a week [後脚の力が強く].
kept.quote: ハイセイコーは後脚の力が強く、「滑らかさよりも力で走る」タイプの競走馬であり、後脚の蹄鉄は装着してから1週間ほどで擦り減ってしまったといわれている
kept.note: The quote is there exactly (競馬 黄金の蹄跡).

kept.description: Body sank lower when he reached top speed [ぐーんと躰が沈みこんでいく], in jockey Masuzawa's words.
kept.quote: 増沢はハイセイコーがスピードに乗った時の感触について、「ぐーんと躰が沈みこんでいく」と表現している
kept.note: The quote is there exactly.

kept.description: Heavy bone. Cannon circumference was measured at 21.5 cm in December 1974 (管囲21.5cm).
kept.quote: 体長163センチメートル、体高…171センチメートル、尻高169センチメートル、胸囲188センチメートル、管囲21.5センチメートル
kept.note: The measurement taken on 21 December 1974 is there. 21.5 cm maps to 1.07 under the vocabulary rule.

kept.description: Pulling, digging foreleg action [かき込むような走り方]. His trainer, Suzuki Katsutaro, cited it as the reason he handled heavy ground.
kept.quote: かき込むような走り方をすることから状態の悪い馬場を苦手とすることはないという見解を示している
kept.note: The quote is there (鈴木勝太郎, trainer after his move to the JRA, per the infobox). It is one person's view, and the moderate 1.15 reflects that.

kept.description: Short below the knee (short cannons), which made him look less refined [膝下が短く]. Candidate parameter for cannon or lower-leg length.
kept.quote: 一方でその馬体は膝下が短く、洗練された気品にはやや欠けていたとも評されている
kept.note: The quote is there exactly.

kept.description: Huge, short-coupled frame: 171 cm at the withers, body length 163 cm, girth 188 cm, over 650 kg as a stallion. Described as compact through the body [胴の詰まった体型] and as running like a heavy tank [重戦車]. Candidate overall-size and body-length parameters.
kept.quote: 体格の大きなハイセイコーの走りは重戦車にたとえられた / 胴の詰まった体型からこなせる距離は1800mまで
kept.note: Both phrases and the measurements are there. The 胴の詰まった remark is the trainer Suzuki's early impression.

kept.description: Occasionally played with his tongue while on the bit, so he raced in a bit lifter [ハミ吊り] from the Satsuki Sho on. A tongue and tack quirk.
kept.quote: 調教中にハイセイコーがハミを噛んではいるものの時折舌を遊ばせることに気づき…対策として陣営は、ハミ吊りを装着することにした
kept.note: The quote is there (after the Spring Stakes, citing 赤木1975). It says 'occasionally played with his tongue', and the bit lifter stops the tongue going over the bit.

kept.description: Toed-out forelegs [外向肢勢]: below the knee the forelegs bent outward, forming an 'A' seen from the front. It worsened with growth until people called him 'bent-legs'. Nijinsky's connections said this was the only way he differed from his sire. Candidate foreleg toe-out parameter.
kept.quote: 前脚が膝下から外に曲がっており、正面からみるとA字になるような形を「外向肢勢」といい、マルゼンスキーはそれに該当したのである / 前脚の膝から下の部分が多少外側に曲がっていた。いわゆる「外向き」。
kept.note: Both quotes are there exactly (Wikipedia, and the Yushun WEB article '記憶の中のマルゼンスキー'). Wikipedia also has '脚曲がり' and '違うのは外向肢勢だけ'.

kept.description: Low centre of gravity; he sank lower as he accelerated [重心が低いから加速するとスーッと沈む], according to his jockey Nakanowatari.
kept.quote: 重心が低いから加速するとスーッと沈むようになる
kept.note: The quote is there exactly, from jockey 中野渡清一 (Number 340).

kept.description: Exceptionally powerful pulling foreleg action [掻き込み]: rivals said clods of dirt came flying back, and on heavy ground he threw mud about three times higher than other horses.
kept.quote: 顔に当たると痛い、砂の塊が飛んで来るんだ。あんな馬はいない。掻き込みがぜんぜん違っていたんだね / 道悪で走ったときの跳ね上げる泥の高さというのが、もう並の高さじゃない。コーナーワークのときなんか、他の馬の3倍ぐらいバーンと跳ね上がる
kept.note: Both quotes are there exactly (小島太 and 野平祐二).

kept.description: Big stride [跳びも大きい], with a very fast return of the extended hind leg. Remark by the trainer's son, who handled his early training.
kept.quote: 「この馬は跳びも大きいけど、伸びた後脚を戻すのがものすごく速い」と感嘆していたという
kept.note: The quote is there exactly (橋本's son, who did his early training). The moderate 1.06 is fair.

kept.description: Long-legged, lanky, unimpressive build [脚が長くひょろっとして]. Candidate leg-length parameter; a thin frame might also suggest a slightly narrower barrel.
kept.quote: 脚が長くひょろっとして見栄えのしない馬体で、入厩後もダート調教での動きが悪かったため、やはり関係者の期待は高くなかった
kept.note: The quote is there exactly.

kept.description: Wore a custom white hood [白い覆面 / メンコ] in the 1984 Japan Cup, his first time in a hood, with extra-thick leather over the ears to act as earplugs against the crowd. Tack and hood quirk.
kept.quote: 特注の白い覆面を用意した。「普通のメンコは、耳の皮が一重。あの雰囲気でウワーッという大歓声に包まれても大丈夫なように、耳だけ皮を厚めにしてもらった。いわば耳栓みたいなもの」 / Wearing a distinctive white hood, Katsuragi Ace went to the front
kept.note: The Hochi article ('秘密兵器は長い手綱と白覆面') has both phrases word for word, and says it was his first hood (初めて装着したメンコ). English Wikipedia has 'Wearing a distinctive white hood'.

kept.description: Very bit-sensitive and keen to pull forward, so in the Japan Cup he was ridden on white reins about 30 cm longer than normal, to keep the bit off his mouth. Rein and tack quirk.
kept.quote: 通常よりも３０センチほど長い手綱の使用は、レースの直前に決めたと西浦は証言する。 / 他馬より明らかに長い白色の手綱 / ハミに対して非常に敏感な馬であり、少し間違えるとすぐに前へ行きたがってしまう癖がある
kept.note: The first two phrases are in the Hochi article and the third is on Japanese Wikipedia, all exact.

kept.description: His whole body sank lower as his speed built [自然に身体が沈み込んでいく], according to jockey Yoshinaga.
kept.quote: 全身がバネのようで、全身を使って走るから凄く乗りやすい。スピードがぐんと伸び出すと、自然に身体が沈み込んでいく。理想的な走り方
kept.note: The quote is there exactly, from jockey 吉永正人 (光栄出版部 1995, p.83).

kept.description: Small, delicate frame (450-465 kg). Tosho Boy's vet first took him for a filly [ちっちゃくて牝馬かと思ったよ / 華奢]. Mapped to fine bone.
kept.quote: シービーは450kgから460kg半ばまでの比較的小柄な馬であった。また体躯の様子も華奢なもので…「ちっちゃくて牝馬かと思ったよ」と語っている
kept.note: The quote is there (vet 猪木淑郎). 華奢 means slight or delicate overall, not bone specifically, so fine bone is a proxy, and a mild 0.93 is fair. A footnote says the slender, filly-like build was common to Tosho Boy's colts.

kept.description: Springy, bouncing 'rubber-ball' action [ゴムまりのような弾むような走り方 / 全身がバネのよう]. It inspired Sugimoto's race call 'the earth bounces, Mister C.B.'. Like the Teio step, it fits no current parameter; candidate 'bounce' parameter.
kept.quote: 走り方も特徴的なシービーは、ゴムまりのような弾むような走り方をしていたこともあり…杉本が「大地が弾んでミスターシービー」と表現していた
kept.note: The quote is there (the Kikuka Sho call).

kept.description: His signature tack was a bit lifter [ハミ吊り], the three-pronged device on his face that kept his tongue from going over the bit.
kept.quote: シービーのトレードマークともなっていたハミ吊りが切れ / 馬が舌をハミの上に出さないようにするための補助装具。冒頭写真顔面部にある三つ叉の装具。
kept.note: Both the text and the footnote are there exactly.

kept.description: Thin, weak hoof walls [蹄が薄かった]; he raced and trained in aluminium shoes. Hoof wall thickness rather than size.
kept.quote: シービーは他馬より蹄が薄かったために、蹄鉄を留める釘を打てる場所が少なく / シービーは爪が非常に薄くて軟弱で
kept.note: Both quotes are there. Aluminium shoes were used in both training and races (常時アルミ製の蹄鉄).

kept.description: Striking, 'human-like' eyes. Jockey Yoshinaga called them his greatest charm and said he never met another horse with eyes like that. The beauty of his eyes was said to pass to his foals, which Shadai's Nakao described as having large, clear eyes. Candidate eye-size or eye-shape parameter.
kept.quote: 吉永は瞳が最大の魅力であるとし、「人間みたいな目で、あんな目をした馬には一度も会ったことがなかった」と語っている / 瞳の美しさは産駒にも受け継がれており…シービー産駒の特徴として「目が大きくて澄んでいる」ことを挙げている
kept.note: The quotes are there, but 'large and clear' (目が大きくて澄んでいる) is said of his foals, not of C.B. himself. For C.B. the source only says his eyes were striking and human-like. I reworded the description so his own eye size is not overstated.

kept.description: Huge stride under acceleration: 8.70 m in the Derby straight, against an average of 7.30 m for Thoroughbreds of the time.
kept.quote: 当時のサラブレッドの平均完歩（7メートル30）を大きく上回る8メートル70のストライド。
kept.note: The quote is in the Sponichi Lega-scene article on the 1984 Derby, and Wikipedia repeats it under '加速時のストライドの大きさ'. The figure is a peak stride under acceleration, but it supports the top of the range.

kept.description: Lowered his centre of gravity as he shifted into top gear in the 1984 Derby straight [重心を低く下げて]. This is a single line in a dramatised newspaper narrative, not a trait a rider or trainer described, so it is given a light value.
kept.quote: 重心を低く下げてギアがトップに入る。
kept.note: The line is there exactly, but it is a one-moment flourish in a dramatised narrative. No jockey or trainer statement backs it, unlike Haiseiko, Maruzensky and C.B. I lowered bodyLow from 0.5 to 0.35 so it is not ranked level with those first-hand reports.

kept.description: Habit, inherited from grandsire Speed Symboli, of raising his head and neck to check his surroundings [首をあげて周りを確かめるしぐさ]. Not a racing head carriage.
kept.quote: 祖父のスピードシンボリの癖だった首をあげて周りを確かめるしぐさは、あの子に受けついでいます
kept.note: The quote is there exactly (松島光好).

kept.description: Strong lead-leg preference: jockey Okabe said he was 'left-handed' [左利き]. He could hold one lead without changing for long stretches and changed leads very smoothly. Candidate lead-preference parameter.
kept.quote: 岡部は引退後ルドルフが左利きであったことを明かし、「他馬が我慢できずに手前を替えるところでも手前を替えずにガマンできる…又、手前の替えも非常にスムーズであった」
kept.note: The quote is there. Okabe's example is holding the right lead from the start to the final corner over Nakayama's 2200 m.

kept.description: A known kicker who was supposed to wear a red kicker's ribbon on his tail [蹴る可能性を示す赤いリボンを尻尾に]. Before the 1988 Mainichi Okan the groom forgot it, and he kicked two horses (Legend Teio and Dyna Actress). The source is jockey Kato's Instagram as paraphrased in a Wikipedia footnote; I could not open the Instagram post. Tail-ribbon tack quirk.
kept.quote: 担当厩務員が赤信号(蹴る可能性を示す赤いリボン)を尻尾に付け忘れ、後ろを歩いていた郷原洋行騎手がレジェンドテイオーを近づけすぎたため、蹴りを入れられた
kept.note: The footnote text is there exactly, citing 加藤和宏's Instagram. The race is the Mainichi Okan of his comeback after Europe (1988), where he kicked レジェンドテイオー and ダイナアクトレス. The primary Instagram post was not re-checked, so this rests on secondhand evidence.

kept.description: Large belly and ribcage [大きな腹袋]. Her groom read it as a sign of strong heart and lung capacity. Mapped to a well-sprung barrel.
kept.quote: 担当厩務員の小島浩三が注目した大きな腹袋は、心肺機能の高さを示唆していた / her groom Kozo Kojima saw that she had a large abdomen
kept.note: The quote is on both pages (『優駿』2021年9月号 p.17). 1.07 is fair.

kept.description: Flaxen chestnut [尾花栗毛] with a golden mane and tail, inherited from his sire Viceregal. It gave him his name and made him one of the best-known 'good-looking horses'. A colour option, not a shape parameter.
kept.quote: 幼い頃から金色のたてがみと尾を持つ「尾花栗毛」であった / その金髪から「ゴールドシチー」と命名され
kept.note: The quote is there on the right page (the 1984-born horse, sire ヴァイスリーガル). English Wikipedia confirms the golden mane and tail.

kept.description: Small, compact, lightweight build that was still very powerful [小柄ながら力も非常に強く / 軽くてコンパクトなボディー]. Overall body size is not in the vocabulary, so this is a candidate for a new 'overall size' parameter.
kept.quote: 小柄ながら力も非常に強く、後年の武は、数々の騎乗馬の内で「一番気の強い馬」「一番パワーのあった馬」として本馬の名を挙げている ... 武は「良くも悪くも、凄まじい推進力を持った馬でしたね。軽くてコンパクトなボディーに、超ハイパワーのエンジンを積んでいた、という感じ」と評し
kept.note: Re-fetched the ja.wikipedia wikitext (racehorse infobox, JBIS ref). Both phrases are there (Take, citing Shimada 1997/2007). The same page also quotes Fukunaga: 「小柄だが精悍でバランスが良い馬だ」.

kept.description: Ran with an action that used the whole body, so he did not look small at speed (jockey Masato Shibata) [体全体を使うフォーム]. No direction is given for any single parameter.
kept.quote: 柴田政人は「体全体を使うフォームで、体の小ささを感じさせなかった」と述べ
kept.note: The quote is there word for word (cites Sports Graphic Number PLUS p.23). It is right to leave it null, because it gives no direction for any one parameter.

kept.description: Once he matured he ran with a low, sinking footwork. Early in his career he had run stiffly with his head thrown up high [低く沈み込むようなフットワーク].
kept.quote: デビュー当初は頭を高く突き上げる硬い走りだったが、本格化以降は低く沈み込むようなフットワークを身につけている
kept.note: Exact text is in the 走法 section (cites 優駿 2012-11 pp.74-75). 0.6 is a fair, moderate value for 'sinking' footwork.

kept.description: His aggressive action never lifted the head and neck until the finish line, and was likened to 'a big dog running' [ゴールまで絶対に首を上げない / 大きな犬を思わせる走法].
kept.quote: その独特なフォームはゴールまで絶対に首を上げない攻撃的な走りと称され、「大きな犬を思わせる走法」という競走馬に対する比喩としては珍しい表現をされている
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 優駿 1989-02). 'Never lifts the neck', together with the low sinking action, supports a moderately low head. -0.5 does not overstate it.

kept.description: Slight, delicate, small frame; his trainer Obara said he looked 'like a girl' [華奢で小柄な馬体].
kept.quote: 外見上の大きな特徴は、脚の長さだけが目立つ華奢で小柄な馬体である。管理する小原調教師をして「女の子のようだ」「とても走る感じじゃなかったね」
kept.note: Exact text found in 特徴/身体 (cites 谷川 2012 p.73 and 阿部 1995 p.89). Reading 華奢 as fine-boned at 0.92 is fair. The 小柄 (small) part would belong to an overall-size parameter if one is added.

kept.description: His legs looked long for his small body; their length was the only thing that stood out [脚の長さだけが目立つ]. Candidate for a new 'leg length' parameter.
kept.quote: 脚の長さだけが目立つ華奢で小柄な馬体
kept.note: Exact text found. No leg-length parameter exists, so null is right.

kept.description: Front legs toed out, which was noted as a conformation fault [前脚に外向].
kept.quote: また、前脚に外向が認められたことも欠点の１つであった
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 阿部 1995 p.89). There is no toe-out parameter, so it stays null.

kept.description: A big-bodied, strong-willed horse, described as 'the boss of the stable' [体が大きく]. Candidate for a new 'overall size' parameter.
kept.quote: 体が大きく、気も強い、厩舎の大将だったのだ。
kept.note: Re-fetched the Number article. It is about the real horse (1989 Yasuda Kinen, Take Kunihiko stable), and the sentence is there word for word, right after he bares his teeth at Osumi Shadai.

kept.description: Always keen to go and pulled very hard. In sprints he was ridden on a long rein with the bit released [常に行きたがる / 長手綱でハミを外しながら乗る]. This is riding behaviour, not anatomy.
kept.quote: レースでは常に行きたがる癖があったが ... それゆえに、気合をつけて追走するのが基本の短距離のレースでは、長手綱でハミを外しながら乗るという方策が取られていた
kept.note: Both phrases are on ja.wikipedia (cites 島田 1995 p.122). The page says his pulling power was so great that Kishi trained in a gym before riding him. This is behaviour, so null.

kept.description: His distinctive action sank his big (500 kg+) body to keep a low centre of gravity, which earned him the nickname 'heavy tank'. English Wikipedia: 'running style in which he stayed low to the ground' [馬体を沈めるように低い重心を保ち / 重戦車].
kept.quote: 500キロを超える大きな馬体を沈めるように低い重心を保ちつつ前肢をかき込むように繰り出すフォームは特徴的で、ファンやメディアはその姿を"重戦車"と例えた。
kept.note: The Yahoo expert article by Hanaoka Takako (2022) covers the real horse's history. It mentions the game only as the news hook, and the sentence is there exactly. English Wikipedia says 'distinctive running style in which he stayed low to the ground'. 0.7 is fair, since both sources single the trait out.

kept.description: Threw the forelegs out with a pawing, ground-raking motion [前肢をかき込むように繰り出す] (掻き込み).
kept.quote: 前肢をかき込むように繰り出すフォームは特徴的で
kept.note: The phrase is there, and the vocabulary itself maps 掻き込み to high kneeAction. The source gives no knee height, though, and Oguri Cap's (stronger) 掻き込み in this batch was left null because he too ran low. The orchestrator may want to treat the two the same way, either both null or both mapped.

kept.description: A big, heavy-framed horse of over 500 kg [500キロを超える大型馬]. His legs were fragile, with weakness in the hip joints, hindquarters and hocks. Candidate for a new 'overall size' parameter.
kept.quote: メジロアルダンは500キロを超える大型馬で、脚元への負担もより大きかった。その体を支える股関節やトモ(後肢の筋肉)、飛節(後肢にある関節)に甘さがあり
kept.note: Exact text found. English Wikipedia also says 'large build, heavy frame'. Size has no parameter, so null.

kept.description: Raced with a very low neck and head: he sank the neck down as he ran. Trainer Tsutomu Setoguchi named the low centre of gravity and low neck position as the defining features of his action [沈むように首を下げ / 重心と首の位置が低い].
kept.quote: オグリキャップは首を良く使う走法で、沈むように首を下げ ... 瀬戸口勉もオグリキャップの走り方の特徴について、重心と首の位置が低いことを挙げている
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 小栗 1992 pp.114-116, 小栗 1994 p.46, 優駿 2010-09 p.53). Several sources say it, and it is his best-known trait, so -0.9 is justified.

kept.description: Carried his body low and parallel to the ground, so from his Kasamatsu days he was called 'the horse that crawls along the ground'. Jockey Katsumi Ando: low centre of gravity and enormous forward drive [地を這う馬 / 重心が低く].
kept.quote: 前後にバランスを取りながら地面と平行に馬体を運んでいく走りから、笠松時代から「地を這う馬」と形容されることがあった。安藤勝己は秋風ジュニアのレース後、「重心が低く、前への推進力がケタ違い。あんな走り方をする馬に巡り会ったのは、初めて」と思ったという
kept.note: Exact text found (wikitext has [[重心]] link markup). 0.8 is fair for a horse nicknamed 'crawls along the ground'.

kept.description: Made big use of his neck, balancing front to back as he ran [首を良く使う走法].
kept.quote: オグリキャップは首を良く使う走法で、沈むように首を下げ、前後にバランスを取りながら
kept.note: Exact text found. 首を良く使う maps directly onto the vocabulary's 首を大きく使う, and 1.3 is not exaggerated.

kept.description: Very strong kick. In each stride he reached the forelegs out to their full extent and floated forward, gaining about 20-30 cm per stride on an ordinary horse [前肢を目いっぱいに延ばし、浮くように跳びながら走る]. The physical gain is only about 3-4% of a ~7 m galloping stride, so this is a modest lengthening.
kept.quote: オグリキャップは肢のキック力が強く、瞬発力の強さは一回の蹴りで前肢を目いっぱいに延ばし、浮くように跳びながら走るため、この走法によって普通の馬よりも20から30センチ前に出ることができた
kept.note: Quote verified (cites 小栗 1992 pp.114-116). Lowered stride from 1.07 to 1.04. The source puts a number on it: 20-30 cm extra per stride, about 3-4% of a typical ~7 m stride. The page never calls him a ストライド走法 or 大跳び horse, so 1.07 overstated it.

kept.description: Very large hooves with thin soles, according to trainer Setoguchi [蹄は「ものすごく大きくて、底が薄い」].
kept.quote: 瀬戸口勉によるとオグリキャップの蹄は「ものすごく大きくて、底が薄い」といい
kept.note: Exact text found in a footnote (cites 優駿 2010-09 p.55). 'ものすごく大きい' (enormously big) justifies the top of the range.

kept.description: Powerful inner thighs and hindquarters 'solid like a carthorse'. His Kasamatsu trainer Washimi: the muscle of his quarters was tremendous [下半身が馬車馬のようにガッシリ / トモの筋肉もグワーッとすごく良かった].
kept.quote: 腿の内側に力があり下半身が馬車馬のようにガッシリしているという印象を受けた / 「そりゃ体形が違ったから、あご張りはいいし『トモ』の筋肉もグワーッとすごく良かった」
kept.note: Both quotes found. The Gifu Shimbun 'Oguri no Sato' column interviews his real Kasamatsu trainer Washimi. One caveat: the same Wikipedia paragraph quotes Kawachi saying his hind legs were not yet firm when he moved to the JRA, but they firmed up by the NZT. So 1.1 is fair for the mature horse.

kept.description: Ran with his ears pricked up. Jockey Yukio Okabe, after the 1988 Arima Kinen: 'this horse runs with his ears up; maybe he is enjoying the race' [耳を立てて走る].
kept.quote: 岡部幸雄は1988年の有馬記念のレース後に「素晴らしい精神力だね。この馬は耳を立てて走るんだ。レースを楽しんでいるのかもしれない」と語り
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 山本 1992 p.168). 耳を立てる means ears up or pricked, the opposite of pinned (耳を絞る), so -0.7 is fair. It is one jockey's remark, but he states it as a general habit ('この馬は…走るんだ').

kept.description: Extremely strong 'raking' of the track with the forefeet. He scraped his heels on the ground until they bled and wore through shoes so fast that his hooves were full of nail holes [馬場を掻き込む力が強く]. Kept as null rather than kneeAction because it goes with his low, ground-skimming action rather than a high knee lift.
kept.quote: オグリキャップは走行時に馬場を掻き込む力が強く、その強さは調教中に馬場の地面にかかとをこすって出血したり ... 蹄鉄の磨滅が激しく頻繁に打ち替えられたために蹄が穴だらけになったことがあったほどであった
kept.note: Text found (cites 渡瀬 1992 pp.265-266 and 山本 1992 pp.180-182). Null is a defensible choice, but it conflicts with mapping Mejiro Ardan's 掻き込み to kneeAction 1.2. The orchestrator should settle on one rule for both.

kept.description: Right foreleg toed out from birth [生まれつき外向していた右脚]. A vet blamed his later suspensory injury on raking the ground hard with that leg.
kept.quote: 栗東トレーニングセンター競走馬診療所の獣医師松本実は、5歳時に発症した右前脚の繋靭帯炎の原因を、生まれつき外向していた右脚で強く地面を掻き込むことを繰り返したことにあると分析している
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 渡瀬 1992 p.342). The Gifu Shimbun article confirms it independently: 「（生まれた時に「外向」だった）右前脚だけは心配した」.

kept.description: Preferred to lead on the right leg, so he ran better right-handed. He also tended to lean or drift toward the inside rail [右手前で走ることが好き / 内側にもたれる癖].
kept.quote: 武豊によるとオグリキャップは右手前で走ることが好きで、左回りよりも右回りのコースのほうがスムーズに走れた。またコースの左右の回りを問わず、内側にもたれる癖があった。
kept.note: Found (wikitext reads 右[[手前]]; cites 武・島田 2003 pp.146-147, 160-161). The Arima Kinen section repeats the 内側にもたれる癖 when cornering.

kept.description: Broad, well-developed jaw/jowls (あご張りがいい), which his Kasamatsu trainer linked to his big appetite. Candidate for a 'jowl width' parameter.
kept.quote: 「そりゃ体形が違ったから、あご張りはいいし『トモ』の筋肉もグワーッとすごく良かった」 ... 「あご張りがいい馬は、（飼い葉などの）食い込みがいい訳だ。」
kept.note: Re-fetched the Gifu Shimbun column (2025-04-18, about the real horse's Kasamatsu days). Trainer Washimi's remark and the appetite link are both there. There is no jowl parameter, so null.

kept.description: Longer in the body (barrel/back) than his full brother Sakura Toko, which made his breeder think he could stay longer distances [胴が長く]. Candidate for a new 'body length' parameter.
kept.quote: また兄サクラトウコウよりも胴が長く、谷岡は長い距離もこなすことではと考えるようになっていた
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 優駿 2002-06 p.59). It is a comparison with his brother as a foal, not with Thoroughbreds in general, so null and moderate confidence are right.

kept.description: Well known for having a big face; manga artist Miho Yoshida used it as a gag several times, including a 'giant-face showdown' with Biwa Hayahide [顔が大きい].
kept.quote: ほか、顔が大きいことがよく知られており、競馬漫画家のよしだみほが幾度が自作のなかで題材として扱っている
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 競馬名馬読本 p.107 and よしだ p.57). The footnote mentions the 巨顔対決 with Biwa Hayahide and says Take always said 'そんなことはないですよ'. Since it is 'well known', 1.12 is fair. If Biwa Hayahide is modelled, he should probably sit at or above this value.

kept.description: Left foreleg toed out and crooked from foalhood, which caused recurring leg trouble [左前脚が外向 / 左前脚に歪み].
kept.quote: 幼駒時代から左前脚が外向していたが ... 身体的には前述の通り左前脚に歪みがあり、これを原因とした脚部不安もつきまとった
kept.note: Both phrases found (cites 週刊100名馬 Vol.5 p.5 and 競馬名馬読本 p.107). There is no toe-out parameter, so null.

kept.description: Big and muscular even as a foal. His trainer Ogino Mitsuo compared him to a 'dump truck', against his stablemate the 'Mercedes' [大柄 / 筋肉質 / ダンプカー]. Candidate for an overall size/mass parameter.
kept.quote: 初仔は、他と比べて大柄だった。筋肉質で / もう1頭のヤエノダイヤが（メルセデス）ベンツなら、ムテキはダンプカーや。
kept.note: Both phrases found (cites 週刊100名馬 p.7 and 優駿 1988-06 p.136). The infobox confirms Ogino Mitsuo was his trainer (調). The dump-truck line is about raw power versus refinement, which fits an overall size/mass candidate.

kept.description: Marked with four white socks and a blaze [四白流星]. This is coat marking, not anatomy, but it is distinctive on a model.
kept.quote: 顔には「流星」が流れ、四本の脚には白い「ソックス」をはいていた（四白流星）
kept.note: Found (wikitext has link markup around 流星 and ソックス). The lead also says 「四白流星の美男子と呼ばれた」. This is a marking, not a build trait, so null.

kept.description: Front hooves did not match. The left fore was normal, but the right fore was only the size of an adult's fist and almost round [右前のツメが大人の拳ひと握りしかなく丸に近い形]. Kept as null because hoof size is set for all four feet at once.
kept.quote: 伊藤は「左前のツメは普通なのに、右前のツメが大人の拳ひと握りしかなく丸に近い形だった」としている
kept.note: Exact text found in a footnote (cites 週刊100名馬 p.30). The main text says 前脚の蹄に左右差がある不安を抱えていた. Ito is trainer Ito Yuji, who inspected her as a yearling.

kept.description: Had a natural habit of running with his neck held high. Writer Akihiko Yoshikawa called the high-necked, half-open-mouthed look 'this horse's pose'. A shadow roll did not fix it; a noseband and bit lifter later did [首を高くして走る癖 / 首が高く口を割りかげん].
kept.quote: 生まれつき首を高くして走る癖があり、全身をうまく使えないため、直線でもう一伸びすることができなかった ... 吉川彰彦によれば「首が高く口を割りかげんだ」状態は、「この馬のポーズ」であると表している
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 優駿 2003-07 p.60 and 1991-12). The page also quotes trainer Umeda after the noseband: 「頭が高くなるのも矯正され」. 0.8 fits the trait itself; a lower value (~0.5) would fit his corrected GI-winning form.

kept.description: Ran at the front with his mouth wide open, which earned him the nickname 'the horse that laughs as he runs' [口を割って走る / 笑いながら走る馬]. Candidate for a 'mouth open at speed' parameter.
kept.quote: ハイペースで先陣を切り口を開けて走る姿から、「笑いながら走る馬」と呼ばれた
kept.note: Confirmed in all three sources. netkeiba: 「ハイペースで先陣を切り口を割って走る様子から『笑いながら走る馬』と称され」. TV Tokyo: 「口を割って走る姿から「笑う馬」と表現されたこともある」.

kept.description: Got his tongue over the bit and stuck it out while racing [ハミを越えて舌を出す / 舌を越す].
kept.quote: さらに、ハミを越えて舌を出すという癖である「舌を越す」現象にも見舞われ、口を開いたまま走り「かかる」一因にもなっていた
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 優駿 2009-03 p.157). The noseband fitted later was meant to stop this.

kept.description: Always wanted to go left, so he drifted out on right-handed tracks and in on left-handed ones [斜行].
kept.quote: ダイタクヘリオスは、レース中に左へ行きたがるようになり、右回りなら外側に、左回りなら内側に斜行するようになった
kept.note: Exact text found (wikitext has [[斜行]]; cites 優駿 2009-03 p.157). This is a behavioural drift, so null.

kept.description: Called 'the big dark-bay body' in a stud-days anecdote [黒鹿毛の巨体]. This is a weak, figurative size indication. Candidate for an overall size parameter.
kept.quote: 雪解けの頃に寝転がり、馬体についた泥が乾いてしまったときには「黒鹿毛の巨体が芦毛のように変身」し
kept.note: The quote is there (cites 優駿 1994-07 p.81), but it is a passing, half-joking phrase from his stud years, and the page gives no racing weights. It is only weak evidence of size, which justifies the low confidence.

kept.description: Well-developed, powerful hindquarters [後駆（トモ）は充実していた].
kept.quote: デビュー戦の時点で504kgと大柄な馬だった。後駆（トモ）は充実していたがその反面前駆が貧しく
kept.note: Exact text found (cites 優駿 2009-06 pp.155-161). Nakano says the same thing in the Sarabure interview: 「前はガタガタだけど、トモは凄い」. 1.12 is fair.

kept.description: Exceptionally strong hind push. Jockey Eiji Nakano said his hind legs stepped under so powerfully that he had to run leaning on the bit [トモ脚の踏み込みがすご過ぎた / トモが強過ぎる].
kept.quote: ガタガタの前に対してトモは良いんですよ。踏み込みがとても良かったので、ハミにブラさがるような感じだったんです。前も出ているんだけど、トモ脚の踏み込みがすご過ぎたですね。 ... トモが強過ぎるために、ハミにぶら下がるようにして走らないと駄目という稀な馬でした。
kept.note: Re-fetched the Sarabure interview (2014-06-19, Nishizuka with his real jockey Nakano Eiji). Both lines are there exactly. 'すご過ぎた / 強過ぎる' supports a near-maximum 1.18.

kept.description: Underdeveloped, weak forehand compared with his strong hindquarters. Nakano said riding him felt 'like a bicycle with a flat front tyre' [前駆が貧しく]. The source does not mention the chest itself, so this is only a mild narrowing of the front end.
kept.quote: 後駆（トモ）は充実していたがその反面前駆が貧しく、中野は「前のタイヤがパンクした自転車に乗ってる感じ」と表現している
kept.note: Quote verified. Raised chestWidth from 0.93 to 0.95. 前駆が貧しい means the whole forehand was underdeveloped, but no source says the breast was narrow. Nakano's own Sarabure words ('前輪がパンクした自転車…前がガタガタした感じの乗り味') describe how he rode, not the chest, and he adds 「前も出ている」. Most of the front/back imbalance is already carried by hindquarters 1.12.

kept.description: Because the front and back were out of balance, he ran 'hanging on the bit', leaning his weight into the rider's hands. Taking a pull unbalanced him, so he was ridden from the front [ハミにぶら下がる走法].
kept.quote: 前後のバランスが取れていないため ... そのためにハミに頼る「ハミにぶら下がる」という走法となり、手綱を引くとたちまち均衡を失って騎手との連携が取れなくなる危険があった
kept.note: Exact text found. Sarabure backs it up too: 「ハミにぶら下がって走る走法だったということもありましたので、あのような競馬スタイルをすることになった」. It has no parameter, so null.

kept.description: Large horse, 504 kg at his debut [504kgと大柄な馬]. Candidate for an overall size parameter.
kept.quote: デビュー戦の時点で504kgと大柄な馬だった
kept.note: Exact text found. Size has no parameter yet, so null.

kept.description: Handsome, refined face. Yutaka Take praised his face and added that 'a strong horse's face is always well-proportioned and small' [顔がいい / 強い馬の顔は必ず整っているし、小さい]. Trainer Ikee's line 「頭も顔立ちもいい」 means 'clever and good-looking' (頭がいい = intelligent), not a small head. The value rests only on Take's general remark, so it stays mild.
kept.quote: また「顔がいい」「強い馬の顔は必ず整っているし、小さい」と述べている。
kept.note: Quote verified (cites 島田 2003 p.148). I fixed the description because Ikee's 「頭も顔立ちもいい」 praises his brains and looks; the same page also says 頭も良い about his intelligence. Only Take's general 'strong horses have small faces' implies a small head, so I eased the value from 0.94 to 0.95 and dropped Ikee from the quote.

kept.description: Big-framed, unlike his dam and brother; his size contributed to sore shins before his debut [母や兄に似ず体が大きかった / ガラ（体格）のある]. Candidate for an overall size parameter.
kept.quote: 「ガラ（体格）のある、いかにも走りそうな馬」 ... 母や兄に似ず体が大きかったために前膝にソエ（すねの骨膜炎）をきたすようになり
kept.note: Both phrases found. The first is groom Hayakawa (citing 競馬ライバル読本 p.25); the second cites 江面 2017 p.211. Size has no parameter, so null.

kept.description: Swaggering walk, 'like a man walking with his shoulders cutting the wind' (trainer Ikee) [肩で風切って歩いている]. This is a walk-gait quirk, not a racing one.
kept.quote: 第一、歩様が他の馬と全然違いますよ。人間で言えば、肩で風切って歩いているように
kept.note: Exact text found in a footnote quoting Ikee Yasuo (cites 島田 2003 pp.74-75). It describes the walk, not the racing action, so null.

kept.description: Heavy-boned: after his successes it was found he had the largest cannon circumference (front-leg girth between knee and fetlock) of his 1987 Mejiro-bred crop, the crop that included Mejiro Ryan and Mejiro McQueen. No figure in cm is given, so the value is an estimate. [同期の中で最も大きい管囲]
kept.quote: 一方で活躍後には同期の中で最も大きい管囲（前脚の太さ{{Efn|正確に言えば「前脚の膝と、球節の中間の周囲」。}}）を有していた事が判明している
kept.note: Quote found word for word in the ja.wikipedia raw text, cited to 優駿 1993-2, 2006-4 and 1992-9. 'Same crop' means the Mejiro farm's 1987 foals (the paragraph compares him with Mejiro Ryan and McQueen). No cm figure exists, so 1.08 is an estimate; it is within reason for 'largest in a strong crop' but should not be read as measured.

kept.description: One theory says his jumping (steeplechase) training built up the muscles of his hindquarters, especially around the loins. His trainer Okubo instead put his improvement down to natural growth. [腰回りをはじめとする後躯の筋肉が強化され]
kept.quote: 障害での練習にて、腰回りをはじめとする後躯の筋肉が強化され、本格化を促したという説が展開されているが、大久保は馬自身の成長であると捉えている
kept.note: Quote is present in the 障害練習、障害転向の意図とその効果 section. The description correctly presents it as an unconfirmed theory that the trainer disputed. The evidence is weak (a theory about why he improved, not an observed trait). 1.05 is a mild reading; this is a candidate to drop if only strong traits are kept.

kept.description: Thick, heavy neck: trainer Okudaira, comparing him with the handsome Mejiro Ardan, found him unrefined, with a thick neck and thick legs. This was his impression of the young horse. [首や脚が太く垢抜けない馬]
kept.quote: 首や脚が太く垢抜けない馬であると感じ、「並の馬で、そこそこの期待」と評価するに留まっていた
kept.note: Quote found in the 幼駒時代 section (cited 江面 1998 pp.49-50), with the comparison to Mejiro Ardan. A thick neck maps fairly to crest 1.2.

kept.description: Thick legs and heavy bone, from the same trainer remark. The farm chose his sire Amber Shadai partly for robust bone. [首や脚が太く]
kept.quote: 首や脚が太く垢抜けない馬であると感じ
kept.note: Same passage. The sire remark is supported too: the farm manager said of Amber Shadai 「骨質が頑丈にできている点が魅力的」. 1.07 is a fair reading for 'thick legs'.

kept.description: Long-legged, broad, imposing frame as a youngster. Elsewhere he is described as having a 'grand build' [雄大な馬格]. [脚長で幅のある立派な馬体]
kept.quote: かつ脚長で幅のある立派な馬体をしており、牧場史上屈指の豊作年であった1987年生産馬の中でも特に高い評価を受けていた
kept.note: Both phrases are present. 雄大な馬格 is writer Goto Masaharu's description in the 人気 section. 幅のある means overall body width, not the chest specifically, so chestWidth 1.06 is a reasonable, modest mapping.

kept.description: Mane kept cropped short, the 'Ryan cut'. After summer itch made him rub his mane off on fences, his groom trimmed it short and it stayed that way. This is a visual trait with no parameter (mane length/style). [ライアン・カット]
kept.quote: 担当厩務員の小島浩三によってたてがみが短く刈り揃えられ、以後これが常態化して「ライアン・カット」と呼ばれた
kept.note: Quote found word for word in その他. The context (夏癬 at the mane roots, rubbing on fences while resting from periostitis at 3, old age count) matches the description.

kept.description: Unusual forehead profile: thoroughbreds of the time usually had a slight hollow between the eyes, but his was flat to slightly bulging. This points toward a mildly convex profile. Source is his groom, via Sports Nippon (Osaka edition, 16 Nov 1991). [目と目の間は…へっこんでない…ちょっと膨らんでいる]
kept.quote: 当時のサラブレッドでは、目と目の間は少しくぼんでいるのが普通だったが、ケイエスミラクルは「へっこんでないでしょ。真っすぐからちょっと膨らんでいるくらい」だと平森厩務員が語っている
kept.note: Quote found word for word, cited to 『スポーツニッポン』大阪版 1991-11-16. The page is about the 1988 Stutz Blackhawk colt (died Dec 1991). The trait concerns the forehead between the eyes, not the nasal bone (a true Roman nose), so a small positive profile value like 0.3 is fair.

kept.description: Hooves with ridges along the hoof wall and small pits along them. His groom guessed it came from poor health while the hooves were growing. This is a cosmetic hoof-surface detail with no parameter. [蹄壁のあたりに筋があり…穴が開いたみたい]
kept.quote: ツメの形について、蹄壁のあたりに筋があり、その筋に沿ってところどころ穴が開いたみたいになっていた。
kept.note: Quote found word for word, cited to Sponichi Osaka 1991-11-17, along with the groom's guess 「ツメの成長期に体調が良くなかったからでは」. It is too small a detail to model.

kept.description: Extremely high foreleg action at speed: unlike ordinary horses, his forelegs swung up as high as the shoulder. Trainer Matsumoto blamed the extra impact for his repeated fractures. [前脚が肩のあたりまで振り上がるほどのフォーム]
kept.quote: 松元によるとテイオーは普通の馬と違って前脚が肩のあたりまで振り上がるほどのフォームであり、それだけ脚にかかる衝撃も大きかった
kept.note: Quote found (cited 河村2015 p.80). Matsumoto links the form to his repeated small fractures, comparing him to a hard-punching boxer. 'Forelegs up to the shoulder' justifies the maximum, 1.3.

kept.description: Stride runner: elastic muscles let him stretch his stride a long way and recover quickly. Okada called him a great horse who 'earned his speed through the reach of his stride'. [ストライドの伸びでスピードを稼いだ]
kept.quote: このような体質だったことでストライドを大きく伸ばすことができ、元に戻るのも速かったとし、「トウカイテイオーは、ストライドの伸びでスピードを稼いだ名馬でした。
kept.note: Quote found (岡田繁幸, 河村2015 p.80). The article also notes he stood out on the hill track even though stride horses usually post poor times there. 1.1 is fair.

kept.description: The 'Teio walk' / 'Teio step'. Before races he walked diagonally forward, lifting his knees high and bouncing rhythmically, with very long, supple pasterns and a hind fetlock that seemed almost to touch the ground. It vanished at full gallop. No parameter covers it (pastern length/flexibility and walk-gait bounce). [テイオー・ウォーク / 鶏跛 / 繋が非常に長く、かつ柔軟]
kept.quote: 斜め前に歩く形で、膝を高く上げ、弾むようにリズム良く歩く姿を指す。トウカイテイオーは、「繋」と呼ばれる蹄と手首・足首の間にある関節が非常に長く、かつ柔軟であった。 / 尋常ではない繋ぎの柔らかさが同馬の類まれなバネを生みだし、お尻が跳ね上がるような独特の歩様は、のちに「テイオー・ウォーク」と呼ばれるようになる。
kept.note: Both quotes found: the ja.wikipedia テイオー・ウォーク section and the netkeiba 'チーム・テイオー' column, which is about the real horse (born 1988-04-20 at Nagahama Farm). The hind-fetlock detail is also in ja.wikipedia: 「特に後脚の球節は地面に付くのではないかと見られたほど柔らかく」, with the 鶏跛 gait and its disappearance at full gallop. This is a strong candidate for a new parameter (pastern softness / walk bounce).

kept.description: Slim build in his early racing days: Yasuda spoke of his 'slim frame', and as a foal he was long-legged and delicate. His body filled out a lot in pre-training, and he was later praised as near-perfect, so keep this mild. [細身の体格 / 脚が長く華奢な身体付き]
kept.quote: あれを味わったおかげで、細身の体格からも大物感がにじみ出てくるような気がした / 幼駒の頃のテイオーは脚が長く華奢な身体付きで
kept.note: Both quotes found (Yasuda Takayuki on his early rides; 幼駒時代). There is counter-evidence: Matsumoto said by the Nibutani training period the body had become 「びっくりするほど良くなっていた」, and Tokutake (Shadai Stallion Station) called his body 「完璧過ぎました」. 0.95 is a mild, early-career reading and is acceptable, but confidence is low.

kept.description: Hind end felt less powerful than the front early in his career: jockey Tahara said the hindquarters were a little lacking next to the superb forehand ('forelegs like Mercedes suspension, hind legs like a Toyota Crown'). Okabe also wanted 'more weight'. Tahara thought the impression probably came from Teio's softness. [後躯がちょっと物足りない]
kept.quote: 全体的な比較で、前躯の素晴らしさに比べると、後躯がちょっと物足りないという印象は残ります」と述べて「前肢はベンツのサスペンションのようだが、後肢は国産のクラウンくらい」と表現し
kept.note: Quote found. The article frames it as early impressions (初期の印象) and adds Tahara's caveat that it probably came from Teio's peculiar softness. A small 0.95 reduction is a fair, unexaggerated reading.

kept.description: Long forelock was one of his trademarks while racing, and the stud deliberately kept it long. No parameter covers it (forelock length). [長い前髪がトレードマーク]
kept.quote: 競走生活中は長い前髪がトレードマークのひとつであったが、種牡馬入り後も多くの見学者が訪れるため、「イメージを壊さないように」との種馬場の配慮で意図的に長めに整えられていた。
kept.note: Quote found (wiki markup [[トレードマーク]] renders as the quoted text), cited to 『優駿』2008年7月号 p.160.

kept.description: Very small horse who ate little, though springy from a young age. No overall body-size parameter exists. [非常に小柄な馬]
kept.quote: 幼駒時代から強い身体のバネを備えていたが、一方で食が細く非常に小柄な馬だった
kept.note: Quote found word for word in ja.wikipedia (柴田1998 p.8). en.wikipedia has the matching sentence: 'He had a powerful spring in his legs from a young age, but he didn't eat much and was extremely small.' This supports an overall-size parameter, if one is added.

kept.description: Well-developed fore- and hindquarters typical of a sprinter, from foalhood; the breeder had mated for a sprinter. [前後躯が発達した短距離馬に特有の馬体]
kept.quote: 幼駒の頃から胴が詰まり、前後躯が発達した短距離馬に特有の馬体をしており、土井が意図した通りの体型で生まれた
kept.note: Quote found word for word (『優駿』1997年11月号 pp.88-89). The breeder Doi deliberately mated Nihon Pillow Winner for a sprinter. 1.08 is a fair reading of 前後躯が発達.

kept.description: Short-coupled (compact, short body/back), the classic sprinter type. No body-length parameter exists. [胴が詰まり]
kept.quote: 幼駒の頃から胴が詰まり、前後躯が発達した短距離馬に特有の馬体をしており
kept.note: Same sentence. This is a candidate for a body-length / coupling parameter.

kept.description: A small horse, per Suzuki Shiori, the Nishikioka Farm staff member who cared for him in retirement. No overall-size parameter exists. [体が小さい馬]
kept.quote: ゼファーは体が小さい馬なのに一生懸命走って成績を残したんだと思うとあらためてすごい馬だなと思います。
kept.note: Quote found word for word on uma-furusato (the page is about the real Yamanin Zephyr, aged 28, at Nishikioka Farm). en.wikipedia/Yamanin_Zephyr was removed as a source because it says nothing about his size. The description now names the speaker (farm staff member Suzuki Shiori).

kept.description: Massive, thickly muscled hindquarters built by hill-gallop (坂路) training. This was his signature trait, behind nicknames like 'Cyborg' and 'child of the slope'. [分厚いトモ]
kept.quote: 最新の施設であった坂路での調教によって鍛え上げられた分厚いトモを持ち、機械の如く正確なペースで逃げを打つことから「坂路の申し子」「サイボーグ」「栗毛の超特急」などと形容された。
kept.note: Quote found in the article lead (ref markup aside; a note glosses トモ as 腰から臀部にかけての筋肉). It is his defining physical trait, so 1.13 is fair. Supporting detail: at birth his hips were so wide he got stuck during delivery (腰幅が広く引っ掛かってしまうほど).

kept.description: Heavily muscled, 'forged' body overall. He was big even as a first foal (expected to be small), and training visibly lengthened his body. No overall-musculature parameter exists. [体は筋肉質 / 鍛え上げられた栗毛の馬体]
kept.quote: 「体は筋肉質だが短距離馬の体型ではない」 / まるでスポットライトを浴びているかのように鍛え上げられた栗毛の馬体が輝いて躍動した。
kept.note: Both quotes found: ja.wikipedia 評価 section (江面弘也) and the uma-furusato column on the 1992 Satsuki Sho. The supporting claims also check out: 「初仔にもかかわらず大柄であった」, and Haraguchi noted 「胴の伸長」 after Toyama's training.

kept.description: Narrow-bodied: trainer Matsuda remembered her as 'a Bambi-like horse, all spindly long legs and no width' when he inspected her as a foal about a month old. She stayed small and slim, so a mild value is used. [脚ばかりヒョロッと長くて幅のない、バンビみたいな馬]
kept.quote: 松田は後に「脚ばかりヒョロッと長くて幅のない、バンビみたいな馬」「くしゃみをすると、その勢いで倒れてしまいそうだった」と回顧している。
kept.note: Quote found (wiki link [[バンビ (映画)|バンビ]] renders as バンビ; cited 『忘れられない名馬100』 p.140). Context shows the remark is about the foal at about 1 month old, when three trainers had already turned her down for being slim. Adult chest width is not documented directly, so the value was eased from 0.92 to 0.95 and the description now says it was a foal-age remark.

kept.description: Small, slim and very long-legged, with her legs growing longer still in training. No leg-length or overall-size parameter exists. She raced at about 420-432 kg. [体が小さく、細身の体格 / 足の長い]
kept.quote: しかし体が小さく、細身の体格だった。西山茂行は「足の長い、大した馬じゃなかった（中略）馬格もなくて。でも筋肉はしっかりしてました」と回顧している。 / 身長が伸びて脚はさらに長くなっていた。
kept.note: Both quotes found. The weight is supported: she ran the Oka Sho at 420 kg, 'her lowest since debut' and 12 kg down from the Tulip Sho (so about 432 kg). The original '420-430 kg' was tightened to 420-432 kg.

kept.description: Small for a colt but very well balanced, per trainer Iizuka. His stable lad Kawashima was worried by how small he was. He ran the 1993 spring Tenno Sho at 430 kg. No overall-size parameter exists. [男馬にしては体が小さい…バランスがいい体型]
kept.quote: 飯塚はライスシャワーの印象について「男馬にしては体が小さい。それもあって大物感はなく…ただ小さいけれど、いかにもバランスがいい体型なので、うまくいけば中堅クラスまではいくかな、と思いましたよ」と述べている
kept.note: Quote found (the ellipsis stands for omitted text; cited 『名馬列伝ライスシャワー』 p.18). The 430 kg for the 1993 spring Tenno Sho is confirmed in the text and the race table. en.wikipedia has 'the horse's small size stood out' (Kawashima) and mentions 'his small frame'.

kept.description: A more muscular version of his sire Sakura Yutaka O, with the same suppleness (per Fujiwara Goro, breeder of the sire). Jockey Kojima also stressed his extremely supple leg joints. No overall-musculature parameter exists. [筋肉質にしたタイプ]
kept.quote: ユタカオーは本当にきれいな馬だったけど、それを筋肉質にしたタイプがバクシンオーだと思う。柔らかさ、スピードのあるところが似ている
kept.note: Quote found in the 身体面の特徴 section. The speaker is 藤原悟郎 of Fujiwara Farm, which bred Sakura Yutaka O; the description now names him. Kojima's remark 「脚の関節がものすごく柔らかくて、コーナーリングもすごくスムーズ」 is also present.

kept.description: Famously big, long head, often joked about. Announcer Sugimoto was struck by his 'huge face', and Abe wrote that it looked far bigger and longer than jockey Okabe's torso. His finder Takayama disputed this, saying the grey coat just made it look bigger, and critic Ito felt it became less noticeable as his body lengthened at four (old age count). [デカい顔 / 顔が大きい]
kept.quote: 身体面の特徴では顔が大きいことがしばしば取り上げられ、チャームポイント、あるいは揶揄の対象となった。 / 騎手の胴体よりも馬の顔の方がはるかに大きく、長く、思わず笑わずにはいられなかった
kept.note: Both quotes found in the dedicated 顔の大きさ section, and Sugimoto's 「デカい顔にです」 is there too. The vocabulary maps 顔がデカい to 1.15, so the maximum stands. Ito's later comment and Takayama's dispute were added to the description for balance.

kept.description: Thick legs as a young horse: trainer Hamada, inspecting him in his foal year, saw him as unfinished, big-headed and thick-legged, 'outside the standard'. [頭が大きくて、脚も太かった]
kept.quote: 体型的にも頭が大きくて、脚も太かった。規格から外れた感じだよね。
kept.note: Quote found in ja.wikipedia. Hamada said it of the foal in autumn of his birth year (「まだ身体ができてない感じだった」), so it is weak evidence for adult bone, and the value was lowered from 1.06 to 1.04. en.wikipedia was removed as a source because it does not contain this remark.

kept.description: Low centre of gravity in his running once he filled out at 4 (old age count; Kikuka Sho), compared to Tanino Chikara by Yamada Masato. [重心の低さはタニノチカラを思わせ]
kept.quote: この時（菊花賞）には春のひ弱さもなく、サラブレッドの一番充実した形の走りになっていた。重心の低さはタニノチカラを思わせ、身体の筋肉はテンポイントを思わせた
kept.note: Quote found (wiki link [[タニノチカラ]] renders as plain text). The speaker is entertainer and racing commentator 山田雅人, which the description now says. It is a single impressionistic comment and may partly reflect his stocky build rather than his action, so a moderate 0.35 is fair. Low confidence.

kept.description: Light racing weight. His race-day weights in the race-record table run from 416 to 446 kg (馬体重 416–446kg). No source I fetched calls him small in prose. A 2011 farm visit put his weight in retirement at 550 kg. So this describes his lean racing condition, not a proven small frame. Overall body size and weight are not in the vocabulary, so this is a candidate for a new size/scale parameter.
kept.note: I re-extracted the table weights from the raw ja.wikipedia wikitext. They are exactly 416–446 kg over 15 starts. Neither ja.wikipedia's prose, en.wikipedia, netkeiba column 44051 nor uma-furusato 33638 calls him small or slight. uma-furusato column 58881 says that at 21, in retirement, his weight was 550kg (馬体重は550kg). I removed the unsourced claim that he was 'well below a typical classic-winning colt' and reframed the trait as light racing weight. Param stays null.

kept.description: A big, well-balanced filly. Yushun calls her build 大柄でバランスのよい好馬体, and her breeder said that at birth she had such a good frame he 'almost thought she was a colt' [牡馬かなと思ったぐらいの]. Yushun records a race-day weight of 470 kg. This is overall size and mass, which has no parameter.
kept.quote: 大柄でバランスのよい好馬体のノースフライトは、クラシックには間に合わず裏開催の新潟でデビューする。
kept.note: The quote appears verbatim on yushunweb 2567. The ja.wikipedia line is the breeder 斎藤's comment at birth: 斎藤によれば…「牡馬かなと思ったぐらいの」好馬体の持ち主であった. The 470 kg figure is not on either cited page; ja.wikipedia's race table has no weight column. It is on yushunweb 2568: ノースフライトはマイナス10㌔の４７０㌔で出走. I added 2568 to the sources. The description is otherwise unchanged.

kept.description: Drifted inward while finishing, in several races: the 1994 Nakayama Kinen (his jockey was suspended for it), the 1995 Yasuda Kinen and the 1995 Tenno Sho (Autumn) [内側に斜行 / 内によれながら]. This is a drift or lugging-in behaviour with no parameter.
kept.quote: サクラチトセオーは、内によれながらも他と段違いの脚勢を見せて
kept.note: All three are confirmed in the raw wikitext. Nakayama Kinen 1994: 終いに並びかけに行った際、サクラチトセオーは、内側に斜行していた…小島の騎乗停止処分のみが課されていた. Yasuda Kinen 1995: 内側に斜行しながらも他を置き去りに末脚を見せて. Tenno Sho (Autumn) 1995: the exact quoted phrase. The page also notes a fourth case, the 1994 Keio Hai Autumn Handicap: 終いで内外によれたが. Candidate for a new drift/lug parameter.

kept.description: Long-bodied as a newborn foal. Writer Tamaki Abe (優駿, June 2004) said the newborn's long-bodied shape and frame were exactly like his sire Tony Bin's [胴長の体形や骨格が父トニービンに「そっくり」]. This was said at birth. As a youngster on the farm, his breeder later called him fine-limbed and unimpressive (細手の、決して見栄えはしない馬). Body/back length is not in the vocabulary.
kept.quote: 6番仔の姿は、胴長の体形や骨格が父トニービンに「そっくり」（阿部珠樹）
kept.note: The quote is verbatim, apart from a ref tag removed between そっくり and 」. It describes the newborn foal on the day of his birth (1990-03-21), not the mature racehorse. en.wikipedia only says his 'body shape was nearly identical to Tony Bin's' and does not mention length. I changed the description to make the timing explicit and added the contrasting farm-era comment (細手). Param stays null, as a candidate for a body-length parameter.

kept.description: Wore a pure-white, ribbon-like braid in her mane [純白のリボン風の編み込みを鬣に]. Together with her chestnut coat like her sire's, it made her a fan favourite called a 'beautiful girl'. This is a grooming/cosmetic trait with no parameter.
kept.quote: 父サクラユタカオーに似た栗毛の馬体に純白のリボン風の編み込みを鬣に着けていたことから女性ファンからの人気が高く
kept.note: Verbatim on ja.wikipedia (line 26). It continues: 「美少女」「グッドルッキングホース」とも形容された. The page is about the real 1990 chestnut filly by Sakura Yutaka O. This is cosmetic, so param stays null.

kept.description: Raced in white tack [白い馬装], which set off her chestnut body. This is tack colour, with no parameter.
kept.quote: 父サクラユタカオーに似た美しい栗毛の馬体に白い馬装、可愛らしい馬名が相まって、一躍人気者となった
kept.note: Verbatim in the uma-furusato column 'ユキノビジンを訪ねて～村田牧場'. It refers to her 1993 move to JRA after the Crocus S win. This probably overlaps with the white mane braid above, so the two could be merged into one cosmetic 'white tack/ribbon' entry.

kept.description: Small-bodied: never weighed more than 442 kg [最大でも442キロの小柄な馬体]. Overall size has no parameter.
kept.quote: 最大でも442キロの小柄な馬体で、短距離戦での追い込みが特徴
kept.note: Verbatim in the lead section. The race table tops out at 442 kg. The page is about the real US-bred Danzig colt trained in Japan. Candidate for a size/scale parameter.

kept.description: Crooked legs [曲がった脚]. Together with his small frame, this is why he sold cheaply as a 2-year-old and drew few mares at stud. This leg conformation fault has no parameter.
kept.quote: 小柄な馬体と曲がった脚のため、父Danzigの種付け料とほぼ変わらない額での落札となった
kept.note: Verbatim (1993 Barretts sale, $105,000). The stud-career section repeats it: 小柄な馬体や脚が曲がっていることもあり…10頭以上の牝馬を集めることはなかった. The source does not say which legs or in which direction, so it cannot be modelled precisely. Neither sentence has an inline citation on Wikipedia.

kept.description: Raced in a white shadow roll over the nose, fitted to stop him shying at his own shadow, and was nicknamed the 'Shadow-roll Monster' [シャドーロールの怪物]. It is equipment, not anatomy, but it is his signature look. No parameter exists for it.
kept.quote: シャドーロールをつけており、そのトレードマークから「シャドーロールの怪物」という愛称で親しまれた。
kept.note: The original quote (シャドーロールはナリタブライアンの代名詞的存在となり、「シャドーロールの怪物」と称された) is not on any of the four cited pages. I searched the raw ja.wikipedia wikitext and the yushunweb and JRA HTML. I replaced it with the real ja.wikipedia lead sentence. Equivalent statements: yushunweb 2964 has いつしか人はナリタブライアンを「シャドーロールの怪物」と呼んだ, and its photo caption reads 白いシャドーロールは最強馬のしるし (the source for 'white'). ja.wikipedia gives the reason: シャドーロールを装着して下方の視界を遮ることによって（疾走中に自分の影を怖がることがないよう）. The JRA Hall of Fame page is titled シャドーロールの三冠馬. The trait itself is solid. Candidate for a tack/equipment option.

kept.description: His jockey Minai felt that when Narita Brian shifted up into a fast gallop in training, he dropped his centre of gravity: 'the front half of the body drops, then it surges forward'. Minai said this felt the same as Oguri Cap [重心を下げて加速 / 体の前半分がグンと落ちて]. It is a rider's sensation at the moment of acceleration in workouts, not a race-form description from observers.
kept.quote: グググッと重心を下げて加速してくる。体の前半分がグンと落ちて、そのあとでギューンと前へ動く。
kept.note: The quote is verbatim, from Minai's first ride (木村2000, p.102). It is the only running-form statement on the page; there are no matches for 低い/フォーム/走法/首を on ja.wikipedia or the yushunweb story06 pages. It describes a transient feel when shifting from 15-15 into a fast canter, felt from the saddle, not a constant visibly low racing posture. I lowered the value from 0.5 to 0.35 so it does not read as an Oguri-level low form on the strength of a single rider impression.

kept.description: His farrier said all four hooves were almost the same size, whereas hind hooves are normally smaller. Stable staff said the hooves were wide and nearly round rather than the usual long oval, with a broad, concave sole [4つの蹄は大きさがほぼ同じ / 幅が広い球型に近く]. The sources describe shape and front/hind equality, not big feet as such.
kept.quote: ナリタブライアンの蹄は幅が広い球型に近く、土踏まずの部分が広くて内側がくぼんでいた
kept.note: Both statements are verbatim on ja.wikipedia. One is the farrier 山口勝之 (石田1998 / 木村1997). The other is from 大久保厩舎 staff (木村1998a p.110): 通常サラブレッドの蹄は縦に長い楕円形の形が多いが…幅が広い球型に近く. Neither says the feet were large overall. 'Wide' justifies only a slight increase, so I lowered the value from 1.05 to 1.03. Hoof shape (round vs oval) and hind hooves matching the fronts would be better captured by a new hoof-shape parameter.

kept.description: Heavy, draft-type build: Keijiro Okawa said he looked more like a horse for pulling a carriage than a racehorse [馬車でも引いていた方が似合うような体つき]. No single parameter fits; heavier bone and crest would be the nearest approximation.
kept.quote: 「競走馬というより、馬車でも引いていた方が似合うような体つき。長い間、馬を見てきたけれど、ああいうタイプがあそこまで強いっていうのは考えられない」
kept.note: Verbatim in the エピソード section (週刊Gallop臨時増刊100名馬 Vol63, p.9). This is one critic's opinion. In the same paragraph, 谷川直子 says the opposite: 「今、サクラローレルほど美しい馬はいない」. 'Heavy' is a fair paraphrase of a carriage-horse type, but treat it as a disputed impression.

kept.description: Large nostrils, noted by trainer Sakai at birth along with very thin, fine skin [鼻の穴が大きくて]. Nostril size has no parameter.
kept.quote: 皮膚がとても薄くきれいな、いい馬だった。鼻の穴が大きくて、馬相が良かった
kept.note: Verbatim. Trainer 境勝太郎 said it just after the foal's birth (優駿 2020年10月号 p.119). It is a newborn observation. Candidate for a nostril-size parameter.

kept.description: As a youngster at the farm he was gangly ('thin, long and ungainly') and walked lifting his hind legs high like a chicken [鳥足]. This was a juvenile walking trait, not documented at racing speed.
kept.quote: 後ろ脚をニワトリのように持ち上げて歩く「鳥足」であった
kept.note: The text is verbatim, but it is a Wikipedia editor's footnote (Efn, 例えば…) explaining farmhand 小島良太's quote 「ひょろとした馬。細くて長い不格好な」, cited to 優駿 2020-10. It applies to his foal/yearling stage only, so the description's caveat is correct. Param stays null.

kept.description: A small, gentle horse, despite his imposing name [小柄なおとなしい馬]. The race-record table shows weights of about 408–458 kg. The article's citation for this is a cartoonist's tweet. Overall size has no parameter.
kept.quote: いかつい名前とは逆の小柄なおとなしい馬で、洗い場から厩舎に戻るのに引き綱なしでも人間のあとをついていったという
kept.note: Verbatim in the エピソード section. The only ref in that bullet is よしだみほ's tweet, so the sourcing is weak. The table weights I extracted run from 408 to 458 kg, mostly 410–435. That is consistent with 'small'.

kept.description: Unlike most Sunday Silence progeny, his forelegs came out stiffly and he ran with a pawing, digging 'kakikomi' action [前脚がかために出るタイプで、かき込む走法]. The source says this put stress on his legs.
kept.quote: フジキセキは前脚がかために出るタイプで、かき込む走法になる。だから、どうしても脚元に負担が掛かってくるのです。
kept.note: Verbatim. The speaker is 徳武英介 of Shadai Stallion Station (優駿 2008年8月号 p.69), explaining Fuji Kiseki's early disappointments as a sire. The vocabulary maps 掻き込み to high knee action, so 1.2 (slightly under the 1.3 maximum) is a fair reading. It is a stud manager's characterization of the horse's type, not race-film analysis.

kept.description: Muscular, with a lot of body volume, in contrast to Sunday Silence's generally slim, long-pasterned offspring [筋肉質で身体のボリュームもある馬]. This describes general muscle mass, so no single parameter fits.
kept.quote: フジキセキは筋肉質で身体のボリュームもある馬です。サンデーサイレンスは全体に細身でつなぎが長く、クッションのいい馬が多いのですが
kept.note: Verbatim, from the same 徳武 quotation (優駿 2008-08 p.69). Yushun web (story73/2576) adds that he went from 472 kg at his debut to 492 kg in the Asahi Hai, gaining about 10 kg per race. Param stays null; a muscle-mass parameter would be a candidate.

kept.description: As a 2-year-old he was keen and pulled hard in races, opening his mouth against the bit [口を割って行きたがる]. This mouth-gaping behaviour has no parameter.
kept.quote: この日もレースがハイペースで流れているにもかかわらず、口を割って行きたがるところがあった
kept.note: Verbatim on yushunweb 2576. It refers to the 1994 Asahi Hai 3-sai Stakes, where trainer 渡辺 and jockey 角田 both named it as a problem: 馬がまだ幼く、どうしても行きたがること. Candidate for a mouth-open/keenness parameter.

kept.description: His trainer Matsuyama said that as a youngster he had a big skeletal frame, clearly different from other horses [骨格が大きく]. This is overall frame size, and it is only documented for him as a youngster.
kept.quote: 調教師の松山康久によると、幼少時は骨格が大きく、ほかの馬とは明らかに異なる特徴をしていたという
kept.note: Verbatim in the デビュー前 section of the page on the real 1995 Satsuki Sho winner by Sunday Silence. The sentence has no inline citation, and the whole article carries an {{出典の明記}} (needs sources) banner, so it is weakly sourced. Param stays null.

kept.description: Exceptionally massive horse: raced at over 550 kg and won the 1995 Sprinters Stakes at 560 kg, the heaviest JRA G1 winner on record; later raced at 580-582 kg [体重550キログラムを超える大型馬 / 最重量級の大型馬]. No single build parameter covers overall body mass, so this is a candidate for a new overall size/mass parameter.
kept.quote: 体重550[[キログラム]]を超える大型馬 ... この時の馬体重は560キロで、[[日本中央競馬会|JRA]]史上最高馬体重でのGI勝利である
kept.note: Both pages are about the real horse. jawiki has the exact lead sentence, the 560 kg / JRA史上最高馬体重でのGI勝利 line, the 580 kg (Swan S) and 582 kg (Mile CS) race weights, and 現役時代は最重量級の大型馬であった. enwiki independently gives 560 kg and the 580/582 kg weights.

kept.description: Idled once in front: if he hit the lead too early he would ease off and look around (monomi), so Take held him in the pack until the last moment [ソラを使う癖 / モノ見をしてしまう / ゴール前では自分から力を緩める]. Not a build trait. It suits an 'idling/looking around when in front' behaviour, such as ears and head turning, in the late stretch.
kept.quote: マーベラスサンデーは早めに先頭に立つと気を抜いてしまう、いわゆるソラを使う癖があった
kept.note: The exact quote is in the netkeiba 1997 Takarazuka Kinen retrospective, followed by 馬群の中で運んで、ぎりぎりに抜け出すのが武豊の選んだ作戦. jawiki adds Take's words (早すぎるとモノ見をしてしまう) and ゴール前では自分から力を緩める傾向.

kept.description: Raced in a trademark red hood. It was hand-knitted by his groom so he could be spotted anywhere [赤いメンコ（覆面）がトレードマーク]. This is equipment, not anatomy, and fits the existing hood patterns.
kept.quote: 競走生活中は赤いメンコ（覆面）がトレードマークであった
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki, which continues: groom 古川 designed it as a 手編みの特製品 so that 「どこにいても所在が分かるように」.

kept.description: Carried his neck low. His breeder said people at the farm kept stroking his nose, so he lowered his head so often that it became a habit and his neck settled low [首が低かった / 首の位置が低くなった]. The source describes his everyday carriage from farm days, not specifically his racing action, so confidence is low.
kept.quote: 首が低かったが、これは牧場では人間が鼻をしきりに撫でていたために首を下げる回数が多く、それが癖になって首の位置が低くなったと川上は述べている
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki, in the farm-era section about the young horse (6番仔), sourced to 優駿 1997年9月号. The mild -0.3 and the caveat in the description are fair: nothing found describes his racing head carriage.

kept.description: Long, free-reaching stride in the stretch, as described for her 1996 Oaks win [伸びやかなストライド]. This comes from one race description, so confidence is moderate to low.
kept.quote: 伸びやかなストライドでラスト200ｍを駆け抜け
kept.note: The JRA-VAN memorial page is about Air Groove (Shift_JIS page). The exact phrase appears in the Oaks narrative, where she beats 桜花賞馬ファイトガリバー by 1.5 lengths. 1.05 is a modest reading of a single race description.

kept.description: Bit at rival horses during races. In the 1996 Tateyama Tokubetsu he suddenly twisted his neck to the right, tried to bite Daiwa Ocean and lost by a neck; he did the same to Sanlife Teio in the Super Dirt Derby [レース中に他の出走馬に噛み付く / 首を右にひねり…噛みつこうとした]. This is a candidate 'lunge/bite at neighbour' running animation.
kept.quote: ウインディは急に首を右にひねり、ダイワオーシャンに噛みつこうとしたのだ
kept.note: The exact quote is in the Famitsu piece. It is a game-site article but explicitly about the real model horse, and it also describes going for Sanlife Teio's flank. jawiki confirms both incidents: the Tateyama Tokubetsu loss to ダイワオーシャン by クビ差 and the Super Dirt Derby bite at サンライフテイオー. netkeiba: 隣の馬にかみつきに行って勝勢を失い2着.

kept.description: Long-legged, eye-catching frame [脚長の好馬体 / 脚も長く、とても見栄えがする馬体]. No leg-length parameter exists yet, so this is a candidate for one.
kept.quote: 美しい栗毛で脚も長く、とても見栄えがする馬体だった
kept.note: The Famitsu quote is exact. jawiki has 生まれたころから脚長の好馬体だった. Both describe him from birth or as a youngster, so this is a foal-era description, but jawiki's 'from birth' wording implies it continued.

kept.description: Raced in blinkers from the 1997 Heian Stakes onward, to keep his mind on racing instead of on biting [平安Sからブリンカーを着用]. This is equipment, not anatomy.
kept.quote: 陣営は年明けの平安Sからブリンカーを着用。レースに集中することができていた。
kept.note: Exact quote is in the netkeiba 1997 February Stakes retrospective. jawiki: 平安ステークス…このレースからブリンカーを着用したことで、レースにも集中できるようになった.

kept.description: Ran with his head carried high and would not take hold of the bit when he first went into training [頭を高くして走る、ハミを取らない]. This is documented for his early career only, before he matured into the Kikuka Sho winner.
kept.quote: 入厩当初は、頭を高くして走る、ハミを取らないなど気性の難しい馬だったという
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki. It describes how he ran when he first entered training, before his debut, which included bolting at the 3rd corner. +0.5 is a fair reading for that period. The source does not say whether the habit persisted, so the early-career caveat in the description is correct and needed.

kept.description: Long, slender legs. Unlike his heavy-boned sire Mejiro Ryan, he had thin, long legs and a small frame [脚が細長く、小型な馬 / 父は骨太]. The source describes him around birth, so confidence is moderate.
kept.quote: 父メジロライアンは骨太で大型の馬だったが、メジロブライトは脚が細長く、小型な馬であった
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki, right after he is described weighing only 49 kg at birth against an average of 55 kg (優駿 2003年5月号). Reading 'thin, long legs' as finer bone (0.93) is fair, and the 'around birth' caveat is accurate.

kept.description: Small horse overall, unlike his big sire [小柄]. This is a candidate for a new overall size parameter.
kept.quote: 父メジロライアンの大柄な馬体とは異なり、小柄であり
kept.note: Exact phrase is in the jawiki lead/background. His race table shows 446 kg at his 1996 debut.

kept.description: Fought the rider at slow paces by running with her head flung up high, at the 1997 Tulip Sho and again at the 1998 Queen Elizabeth II Cup [首を高く上げながら走り / 首を上げて折り合いを欠いた]. This happened in the early, slow-paced part of races before she settled, not as her normal racing carriage.
kept.quote: 抑えようとする吉田の手綱に反して首を高く上げながら走り、3着に敗れた
kept.note: Quote verified in jawiki (1997 Tulip Sho). The 1998 EQII line says やはり首を上げて吉田との折り合いを欠いた but then しかしじきに落ち着くと. The head-high running was transient, in the slow early pace while she fought the rider. A static +0.4 would apply it to her whole stretch run, so I lowered it to +0.2. The behaviour itself belongs with the head-toss candidate below.

kept.description: Gaped her mouth open and repeatedly tossed her head when pulling hard [口を割って何度も頭を上げる]. This is a candidate for mouth-open and head-toss animation flags.
kept.quote: 口を割って何度も頭を上げるなど折り合いを欠いて制御不能
kept.note: Exact phrase is on the 優駿 web story page, describing the super-slow pace (first 3F 38.3) of the 1997 Tulip Sho.

kept.description: Short-coupled, speed-type build. Her trainer said her siblings were long-bodied stayer types but she looked shorter through the body [胴の詰まった…スピードタイプの体型]. This is a candidate for a body-length parameter.
kept.quote: しかしドーベルはもう少し胴の詰まった印象で、兄や姉よりもスピードタイプの体型に見えました
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki, attributed to trainer 大久保洋吉. It contrasts her with siblings that were 少し胴の長い…ステイヤータイプ.

kept.description: Large-framed. Arthur Hancock III recalled her as a big, splendid yearling [大型で素晴らしい馬]. This is a yearling description only. It is a candidate for an overall size parameter.
kept.quote: アーサー・ハンコック3世]]は当時の本馬について「大型で素晴らしい馬でした」と回想している
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki (from 『衝撃のサンデーサイレンス』 p.11). It refers to her four months at Stone Farm, Kentucky, before she was shipped to Japan in November 1995, so it is a yearling description. jawiki gives no race-day body weights to confirm adult size, so low confidence is right.

kept.description: Filled out across the front as a 4-year-old (old age system): broader shoulders, a thicker chest and stronger muscle, and the body gained width overall [肩は広く、胸は厚く / 全体に幅が出て / 体に幅が出て]. This is growth relative to his own slender younger self; overall he stayed a light, slight horse.
kept.quote: 5歳になってから体重が増えただけでなく肩は広く、胸は厚くなって筋肉も強靭になり
kept.note: All three quotes verified: jawiki (肩は広く、胸は厚く), 優駿 web (全体に幅が出て), and trainer Hashida in Nikkan Sports (古馬になると体に幅が出て). But this is growth compared with his earlier self. His lifetime peak was only 452 kg, and jawiki quotes 野平祐二 calling him 華奢な体型. A chestWidth above the average Thoroughbred (1.06) overstates it, so I lowered it to 1.02.

kept.description: Exceptionally supple, springy body. Before the Yayoi Sho he slipped under the front door of the starting gate, something trainer and writer agree a normal horse could not do [体が柔らかい、バネがある / 体の柔らかさ]. This is a candidate for a spine-flex or suppleness running parameter.
kept.quote: 小さい馬とはいえ、あの狭い隙間をくぐり抜ける体の柔らかさには驚きました
kept.note: Exact quote is in trainer Hashida's Nikkan Sports column. Number p.5: 他の馬とは比べものにならない体の柔らかさがあったからこそできた芸当で、普通の馬はやろうとしてもこんなことはできない. jawiki quotes 上村: 体が柔らかい、バネがある.

kept.description: Famous stall vice: spun round and round to the left in his box for long periods, especially when tense [旋回癖 / 左へぐるぐる回り始めます]. This is a candidate idle animation.
kept.quote: 緊張すると左へぐるぐる回り始めます
kept.note: Exact quote is in the Nikkan Sports column. jawiki: 馬房で長時間左回りにクルクル回り続ける癖, dating from weaning. Number p.4 covers the 旋回癖 and the failed tyre and tatami fixes.

kept.description: Small, light horse. He was 'small and delicate' at birth and peaked at only 452 kg [小さい馬 / 小さくて、華奢で]. This is a candidate for an overall size parameter.
kept.quote: 生まれたときは「小さくて、華奢で、可愛くて」と、稲原は振り返る
kept.note: Exact quote is on Number p.3. jawiki: 生涯最高体重となる452kg (Mainichi Okan), plus 体は小さいけど (Take) and 華奢な体型 (Nohira). Nikkan Sports: 小さい馬とはいえ.

kept.description: Awkward on right-handed tracks: in the 1998 Nakayama Kinen he hung inward in the straight and struggled to change leads, and Take preferred him going left-handed [内側にモタれた / 手前を替えることにも苦労 / 右回りでの不器用さ].
kept.quote: 直線に入るとやや内側にモタれたものの … 右回りでの不器用さを露呈するレースにもなった
kept.note: Both fragments are in jawiki's Nakayama Kinen paragraph (sourced to 『追悼 サイレンススズカ』), along with 手前を替えることにも苦労. The 左回り section quotes Take: 「左回りのほうがいい競馬をする。競馬をしやすい」.

kept.description: Chronic habit of drifting and leaning left in races. He was disqualified from the 2001 Kyoto Daishoten after cutting across Narita Top Road, and the stable fought it with a bit lifter and a one-sided (left-eye) blinker [左への斜行癖 / 左にモタれる / 左にヨレる]. In the 2001 Hong Kong Vase he drifted right instead. This is a candidate 'lateral drift' running parameter.
kept.quote: いつもは左に斜行していく癖があるのに、このふたつのレースだけは、そんなそぶりさえ見せなくて。
kept.note: Quote verified in 週プレNEWS (Take). jawiki has a whole 斜行癖 section on ハミ吊りや片面ブリンカー, and 優駿 web has 左にモタれようとしたり. But the disqualification was in the 2001 Kyoto Daishoten, not 2000: jawiki places it in the 2001 season after that year's Takarazuka Kinen, and its race table lists 京都大賞典 失格 after the 2001 rows. I corrected the year and added the right-drift detail from jawiki.

kept.description: Very small horse: 408-436 kg in races, about 15.3 hands at maturity [小柄な体躯]. This is a candidate for an overall size parameter.
kept.quote: ステイゴールドは最も重かったときで2001年の日経新春杯時の436kgと、小柄な体躯の持ち主であった
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki. The 408 kg minimum is in Katsumi Yoshida's quoted note (最小馬体重は4歳春の日経賞出走時で、なんと408kg). enwiki: 15.3 hands at maturity and a 436 kg maximum.

kept.description: Fine, delicate frame: his groom said his skeleton was 'like a filly's', and Katsumi Yoshida called his build delicate [骨格が牝馬みたい / 馬体は華奢].
kept.quote: 厩務員の山元重治は「骨格が牝馬みたいやった」と評している
kept.note: Both are in jawiki: 山元重治 「骨格が牝馬みたいやった」 and 吉田勝己's 会報 note 馬体は華奢でも、並外れたバネと勝負根性. 0.92 is a fair reading of a filly-like, fine skeleton.

kept.description: Quick-turnover footwork backed by supple muscle, as described by Shigeyuki Okada [回転の良いフットワーク]. This suggests a pitch-leaning action, but the mapping is an interpretation.
kept.quote: ステイゴールドの良さは「回転の良いフットワーク」とそれを支える筋肉の柔らかさにあるとしている
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki (岡田繁幸, from 『ステイゴールド永遠の黄金』). 回転の良い (good turnover) leans toward a pitch action, and 0.95 is a mild reading. It remains an interpretation, so low confidence is appropriate.

kept.description: Powerful, free-flowing long stride [力強くノビノビと走るストライド].
kept.quote: 500kg近い雄大な馬格と、力強くノビノビと走るストライドは、大きな評判を集めていた
kept.note: Exact quote is on the JRA-VAN memorial page for Taiki Shuttle, describing his reputation before his debut was delayed to April of his 3-year-old year. 1.06 is a modest reading.

kept.description: Powerful running action suited to heavy ground and European turf [パワフルな走法]. Mapping 'powerful' to hind push-off is an interpretation.
kept.quote: 雄大な馬格とパワフルな走法。それが力のいるダートにも強かった理由だが
kept.note: Exact quote is in the netkeiba column, which repeats it for the heavy-ground 1998 Yasuda Kinen (そのパワフルな走法が苦手とするはずがなく). The source never mentions the hindquarters, so hindDrive is an interpretation. 1.08 is modest and fine at low confidence.

kept.description: Big, imposing frame of nearly 500 kg [雄大な馬格]. This is a candidate for an overall size parameter.
kept.quote: 雄大な馬格に似合わぬ尾花栗毛の甘いマスク
kept.note: Exact quote is on 優駿 web 755. JRA-VAN: 500kg近い雄大な馬格. netkeiba: 雄大な馬格とパワフルな走法.

kept.description: Flaxen chestnut: a chestnut coat with a golden mane and tail, and a large white star [尾花栗毛 / タテガミ、尻尾が金色]. This is coat and mane colour, not a shape parameter.
kept.quote: 同馬は栗毛であるが、タテガミ、尻尾が金色の[[栗毛|尾花栗毛]]である
kept.note: Exact quote is in jawiki, whose infobox gives 栗毛（尾花栗毛）. enwiki: a flaxen chestnut horse with a large white star. Sports Hochi (2022) headline: 美しい尾花栗毛.

kept.description: Playful hops in races: according to Yukio Okabe he would hop over holes and shadows on the track mid-race, 'running while playing' [穴ぼこや影を見つけるとポンって飛ぶ]. This is a candidate occasional 'shadow-jump' running animation.
kept.quote: あの馬は余裕があるもんだから、レース中でも穴ぼこや影を見つけるとポンって飛ぶんだ。遊びながら走ってる
kept.note: Exact quote is on 優駿 web 755, attributed to 岡部さん (Yukio Okabe) looking back 20 years.

kept.description: His conformation was described as perfectly balanced, with none of the distinctive features most top horses have [均整がとれていて…欠点もない / 特徴のなさが最大の特徴]. This is documented support for leaving his build at the defaults, not a new parameter.
kept.quote: その特徴のなさが、エルコンドルパサーの最大の特徴と言えるのだろう。すべてに均整がとれていて、馬体はしっかりとしており、欠点もない。
kept.note: Re-fetched ja.wikipedia (real horse article). The quote is there word for word. It is writer 後藤正俊 (『優駿』Sept 2000), reacting to 徳武英介 of Shadai Stallion Station, who said the horse showed none of the usual individuality. Leaving the build at the defaults is the right reading.

kept.description: During the 1999 campaign in France his running action adapted to the softer, deeper European turf, his muscling changed, and his body became long and slim [胴長で細身の馬体]. This is a candidate for a body-length parameter; it could also be read as a slightly slab-sided barrel (about 0.95).
kept.quote: やがてそうした馬場に合わせた走法に変化していき、それに伴い筋肉の付き方も変わり、胴長で細身の馬体となっていった
kept.note: The quote is in ja.wikipedia (the 1999 France section, citing 『優駿』). It describes a change during the European campaign, not his lifelong build. Keeping param null as a body-length candidate is fair.

kept.description: Trainer Ogata picked him at the Keeneland sale partly because his hindquarters were exceptionally well developed [後躯の発達が非常によかった]. netkeiba also describes 'powerful hindquarters' and says he was 'known for his muscular build'. He raced at 480–530 kg.
kept.quote: それから後躯の発達が非常によかった
kept.note: Both sources say it. ja.wikipedia quotes Ogata (『優駿』Feb 1998), and netkeiba says 'powerful hindquarters' and 'known for his muscular build'. The weight range checks out: 480 kg in the results table, and 512/530 kg in the text. 1.1 is a fair reading of 'exceptionally well developed' together with 'muscular build'.

kept.description: High-set hocks and a very sloping shoulder [飛節の位置が高い / 肩が非常によく寝ている]. Neither fits the vocabulary, so this is a candidate for a shoulder-angle or hock-height parameter.
