kept.quote: 具体的には飛節の位置が高い馬だったこと、肩が非常によく寝ていること、全体のバランスがいいこと
kept.note: The quote is exact in ja.wikipedia, and netkeiba agrees ('high-set hocks, sloping shoulder ... overall balance'). Note this is how he looked as a yearling at the sale. Param null is correct.

kept.description: He ran with a high head carriage [頭の高い走り]. A column on his 2000 Takamatsunomiya Kinen win names this as his signature, alongside his green shadow roll and hood. Japanese Wikipedia adds that many of his offspring also have a high-necked running style [首の高い走法の産駒も多い].
kept.quote: 緑のシャドーロール、緑の覆面。そして、頭の高い走り──。
kept.note: The uma-furi column is about the real horse (Sakaguchi stable, Fukunaga, the 2000 Takamatsunomiya Kinen) and the quote is exact. ja.wikipedia has 'また首の高い走法の産駒も多い' in the stud section, and 自身と同様 in the previous sentence implies he ran that way himself. 0.5 is a fair moderate value for a trait presented as his identifying feature.

kept.description: A small, slight, delicate filly [小柄な…牝馬 / 繊細]. She weighed only 414 kg at the Tulip Sho, where her weight had dropped [414kgと細化]. Overall size is not in the vocabulary, so this is a candidate for an overall-scale parameter.
kept.quote: 「胡蝶蘭」と名付けられた小柄な鹿毛の牝馬は、その可憐な花のように繊細だった。
kept.note: The uma-furi quote is exact, and the same column says '小柄な馬体に２，４００ｍが堪えた' about the Oaks. ja.wikipedia has '馬体重は414kgと細化'. Her race weights in the ja.wikipedia table run 414–430 kg. One minor point: ja.wikipedia gives her coat as 黒鹿毛, while uma-furi says 鹿毛; this does not affect the trait.

kept.description: As a youngster her hindquarters were very weak [後躯が非常に貧弱], to the point that people doubted she would make a racehorse. They improved once she was in training at Ritto [後躯の状態が良化], so treat this as only a mild trait at racing age.
kept.quote: また後躯が非常に貧弱で、競走馬にはなれないのではないかとも見られていた
kept.note: The quote is exact in ja.wikipedia. en.wikipedia confirms both 'her hindquarters were extremely underdeveloped' and 'the condition of her hindquarters improved'. The only evidence comes from her time as a foal, and the sources say the weakness improved, so nothing documents it at racing age. 0.95 is mild and does not exaggerate, but stay at low confidence; 0.97 is also defensible.

kept.description: His forelegs turned inward [前脚が内側に曲がっていた], like his dam Vega's but less severely. Leg deviation is not in the vocabulary, so this is a candidate for a toed-in / knee-deviation parameter.
kept.quote: 母ベガを吉田和子が所有するきっかけとなったのは前脚が内側に曲がっていたことだったが、仔も母ほどではないが曲がっていた
kept.note: The quote is exact in ja.wikipedia (citing 『優駿』1999). The same paragraph calls his legs '少し曲がった脚', which confirms it was mild. Param null is right.

kept.description: Fine-boned and slight. Trainer Hashida said Sunday Silence foals are never heavy-boned, but even so this colt was small and delicate [小ぶりで華奢]. This describes him as a youngster.
kept.quote: サンデーサイレンスの仔は骨太には出ない（中略）が、それにしても小ぶりで華奢
kept.note: The quote is exact. 華奢, set against 骨太には出ない, does point to a fine frame and fine bone. His racing weight peaked at 464 kg (en.wikipedia), which supports the trait lasting into his racing career. 0.92 is a fair reading.

kept.description: Small for a colt, with a maximum racing weight of 464 kg. This is a candidate for an overall-scale parameter.
kept.quote: He was smaller than average for a male Thoroughbred, with a maximum racing weight of 464 kg
kept.note: The sentence is exact in en.wikipedia (citing JBIS race records). ja.wikipedia also says '初仔のために体は小さく'.

kept.description: A very small mare: 397 kg at her debut [体格的には小柄な馬]. Her trainer Muneishi and others were struck by how small she was, and her regular jockey called her frail [貧弱]. This is a candidate for an overall-scale parameter.
kept.quote: 体格的には小柄な馬である
kept.note: The full sentence in ja.wikipedia is 'デビュー戦における馬体重は397キログラム であり、体格的には小柄な馬である'. Muneishi and Fujiwara both remarked on how small she was, and Furukawa called her 貧弱. Every part of the description is supported.

kept.description: Thin pasterns [繋ぎが細い]. On seeing them, her trainer predicted she would never grow much. This indicates fine bone.
kept.quote: 宗石は加えて繋ぎが細いのを見て、「年をとってもそれほど大きくならない」と感じたという
kept.note: The quote is exact. 0.9 is the bottom of the scale, which is justified for a mare in the 390 kg range with thin pasterns. Note that Muneishi also said she was sound despite her size (小柄ではあるが丈夫な馬).

kept.description: In races she would suddenly try to pull up just when she looked like getting there [ピタッと、突然に止まろうとする], or stop running in the straight. Jockey Furukawa put this down to a cracked left hoof that hurt when she changed leads on the turns. This is a candidate behavioral running quirk (sudden stop).
kept.quote: 「行けると思ったときに、ピタッと、突然に止まろうとする」「直線に向いたら動かないこともある」
kept.note: The quote is exact. The cause is also in the article: '左の爪に裂蹄を発症し、コーナーで手前を変えると痛いときもある'. Note that the same section quotes Muneishi and Furukawa saying she always tried hard, so this is not a temperament quirk.

kept.description: He ran with a big, long-reaching action [大きなフットワーク], which produced his sustained finishing run. The JRA column calls this his greatest weapon.
kept.quote: 大きなフットワークから繰り出す息の長い末脚が、ナリタトップロードの最大の武器だった
kept.note: Re-fetched the archived JRA column 'ひたむきに夢を追って ナリタトップロード'. The quote is exact, and it continues 'スパッとは切れないかわりにジワジワと確実に伸びて', which fits a long-striding horse with stamina. 1.07 is a fair reading, a little short of the 1.1 maximum.

kept.description: A big, imposing frame [雄大な馬体]. netkeiba records racing weights of 478–506 kg. This is a candidate for an overall-scale parameter.
kept.quote: 栗色に輝く雄大な馬体
kept.note: The phrase is in the same JRA column. The netkeiba results page (the right horse) shows race weights from 478(-6) to 506(+8), which matches the stated range. That range is only moderately above average, so any future scale value should stay modest.

kept.description: Owner Takezono bought him on sight because of his big hips and quarters [腰が大きく]; netkeiba says 'strong hindquarters'. This assessment was made when he was about 10 days old.
kept.quote: 腰が大きく、骨がしっかりしていて、繋も柔らかい。
kept.note: The quote is exact in ja.wikipedia (Takezono). netkeiba has 'about ten days after his birth ... strong hindquarters, solid bone, flexible pasterns, and overall balance'. It is a foal assessment only, and Sugimoto's 'not imposing' remark weighs against a big value. 1.06 is suitably mild.

kept.description: Solid, sound bone [骨がしっかりしていて]; netkeiba says 'solid bone'. This comes from the same foal assessment. He also had flexible pasterns [繋も柔らかい].
kept.quote: 腰が大きく、骨がしっかりしていて、繋も柔らかい。
kept.note: Same verified quote. The ja.wikipedia section '心臓と骨の強さ' adds only that his bones showed no left/right difference. It says nothing about heavier bone, so 1.05 should not go higher.

kept.description: Announcer Kiyoshi Sugimoto said his physique did not look powerful or imposing [馬体から迫力を感じる馬ではない], so keep him at an average overall size. His exceptional heart (about 7 kg, resting rate 25 bpm) is internal and not modelled.
kept.quote: 「馬体から迫力を感じる馬ではない」
kept.note: Sugimoto's quote is exact. The heart figures are also confirmed in ja.wikipedia: about 7 kg (心臓は約7kg), and a resting rate of 25 per minute (安静時心拍数は…25回/毎分).

kept.description: A slight, narrow-bodied horse [線の細さ / 細身]. He was the smallest and slimmest of the yearling candidates [最も小柄かつ細身], and as late as early 2000 jockey Matoba said he was still too slight. netkeiba: 'Matoba was initially concerned by the colt's thin frame'.
kept.quote: 的場によれば未だ線の細さが解消されておらず
kept.note: All three phrases are exact in ja.wikipedia: 最も小柄かつ細身, その線の細さに「大丈夫かな、こんな弱々しい体で…」, and 未だ線の細さが解消されておらず. netkeiba has 'smallest and most lightly built' and 'thin frame'. On netkeiba his race weights stayed light for a colt (438–472 kg), so the slightness lasted. 線が細い means slight overall, so barrel is an approximate fit, but 0.94 is mild and fair.

kept.description: He started out short-coupled, looking like a sprinter [胴が前後に詰まった], then grew into a slender, rangy horse [すらりとした姿] once serious training began. This is a candidate for a body-length parameter.
kept.quote: 当初は胴が前後に詰まった短距離向きと思わせる体つきをしていたが、競走年齢の2歳に達し本格的な運動が始まった頃からすらりとした姿に変貌していった
kept.note: The quote is exact in ja.wikipedia. netkeiba agrees: 'At first his compact body suggested a short-distance type, but ... he changed into a more balanced, rangier horse'. The racing-age trait is the rangy build, which suits a body-length candidate.

kept.description: Habitually lugged/drifted inward (the opposite of running straight) when asked for an effort in the straight [内によれる癖 / 内にもたれ / ささる]; in the Kobe Shimbun Hai he wove out then in. A ring bit was fitted for the Kikuka Sho to stop it. Candidate for a new 'drift/lug' parameter (direction: inward).
kept.quote: 本番の菊花賞では内によれる癖を出さないようにリングハミを装着し / 直線では内にもたれ気味になりながらも / 直線へ入るとどういうわけか外へヨレたかと思えば、今度は内へモタれるなどヨレヨレとした走りに。 / スパートをかけると、斜め内側に走ってしまう癖があったのです。競馬用語で言うと「ささる」。
kept.note: I re-fetched all four pages and each one is about the real 1997 colt (the 2000 Satsuki Sho and Kikuka Sho winner). Every quoted fragment appears word for word. The Tokyo Sports note also describes him lugging in after the whip in the Derby and the King George ('またささってる！'), so this is a well-documented, recurring trait.

kept.description: Unsteady, wobbling head/neck carriage noted while galloping past the stands on the first lap of the Kikuka Sho [首をフラフラさせていました]. Seen in one race only.
kept.quote: スタンド前を通過するシャカールは首をフラフラさせていました
kept.note: The quote is word for word in the Tokyo Sports note, in its account of the 2000 Kikuka Sho. It is still a one-race observation, so confidence stays low. The same article says he was 'フラフラと走りながら' in the King George straight, which is closer to wandering than to neck carriage.

kept.description: Pre-race 'tap dance': once saddled he got so wound up that he could not walk normally and jig-jogged as if tap-dancing, so he needed two handlers in the paddock [タップを踏むような歩様 / チャカチャカ / 二人引き]. This is a walking/paddock gait quirk, not a racing-gait one.
kept.quote: 装鞍をするとカッカして普通に歩けなくなり、名前の通り“タップ”を踏むような歩様になってしまいました / 名前のとおり、レースに行く前にはまるでタップダンスを踏むように、ずっとチャカチャカしていた
kept.note: Both quotes appear word for word: the first in Number, the second in Yushun (quoting trainer Sasaki). Yushun also confirms the '二人曳き' in the paddock. Japanese Wikipedia independently says the paddock '二人引き' was there to prevent the 'タップダンス'. All three pages are about the real Pleasant Tap colt.

kept.description: In his early career he tended to bolt or drift toward the outside in races [外側への逃避癖]. Candidate for a 'drift/lug' parameter (direction: outward).
kept.quote: その気性からレースで出遅れたり、外側への逃避癖を見せて敗退を繰り返していた
kept.note: The quote appears word for word in Japanese Wikipedia (citing Sasaki), in the passage explaining his slow rise through the ranks. It is correctly limited to his early career.

kept.description: Big, imposing frame of over 500 kg [500㌔を超す雄大な馬体]. This is overall body size, and no listed parameter covers it.
kept.quote: ５００㌔を超す雄大な馬体は見栄えがして
kept.note: The quote is word for word in the Yushun story. Leaving param null is correct, because this is overall size or weight rather than a specific body part.

kept.description: Early in her career she lost races because she lugged inward and could not run her race [内へもたれて]. Minor and early-career only. Candidate for a 'drift/lug' parameter.
kept.quote: 内へもたれての思うような走りができずに敗れる
kept.note: The quote appears word for word on the Japanese Wikipedia page for the real mare. It sits in a list of reasons for the six-race losing run after her debut, which supports describing it as minor and early-career only.

kept.description: Tended to lean or drift to the right [右にもたれる面]. Trainer Oneda had him tack across to the outside (right-hand) rail on Niigata's straight 1000 m course so he could lean on it. Candidate for a 'drift/lug' parameter (direction: right).
kept.quote: 右にもたれる面のある馬だったから右のラチを頼らせたかった。
kept.note: The quote is word for word in the Chunichi Sports column (1 Aug 2023), from trainer Oneda looking back on the 2002 Ibis Summer Dash record run. The article also says he 'スタートして大外のラチ沿いへ進路を切り替えていった'. It is about the real horse.

kept.description: Stiff action when cantering to the start, yet he ran brilliantly once out of the gate [返し馬でも走りが硬くて], according to his regular jockey Naohiro Onishi.
kept.quote: 返し馬でも走りが硬くて、大丈夫なのかと何度も思いましたが、ゲートを出るとすごい走りをした馬でした
kept.note: The quote is word for word in Nikkan Sports (7 Feb 2024, his obituary), from Onishi. Onishi also says he was 'ものすごくおとなしかった' in the warm-up. This is warm-up stiffness only, so leaving it off the race-gait parameters is correct.

kept.description: Wide, broad hindquarters were the first thing his trainer noticed [トモ幅のある馬].
kept.quote: トモ幅のある馬だな、と思ったくらいで、ここまで走ってくれるとは正直、考えもしなかった
kept.note: The quote is word for word on Japanese Wikipedia, from trainer Yamauchi. 1.08 is a moderate value for 'broad behind' and does not overstate it.

kept.description: A muscular, round, barrel-bodied type with a solid belly, like other Brian's Time colts [腹袋がしっかりとしている、コロンとしたタイプ / でっぷりとした身体].
kept.quote: 筋肉質で腹袋がしっかりとしている、コロンとしたタイプだったよ
kept.note: The quote is word for word (Tomioka). The same page also has 'でっぷりとした身体' (Yamauchi) and the breeder's 'お腹はボテッとしてくる', so a rounder barrel is a fair reading and 1.07 is reasonable.

kept.description: Grew heavier-boned as he matured [骨が太くなってきて], according to his breeder.
kept.quote: 成長するにつれてだんだんと骨が太くなってきて。
kept.note: The quote is word for word (breeder Nobuoka). No cannon-circumference figure was found, so 1.07 is an estimate. It still fits the remark, which is about his heavy, unrefined build.

kept.description: His face grew big as he matured [顔は大きくなるわ], according to his breeder.
kept.quote: 顔は大きくなるわ、お腹はボテッとしてくるわで、決して見てくれのいい馬じゃなかったですね
kept.note: The quote is word for word (Nobuoka). 1.06 is a modest value and does not exaggerate the remark.

kept.description: Short below the knee (short cannons), like other Brian's Time progeny, but with unusually long, relaxed pasterns for the line [膝下は短かった / 繋ぎの部分が...ゆってりしていた]. Candidate for new cannon-length and pastern-length parameters.
kept.quote: 多くのBT産駒と同様に膝下は短かったんだけど、クッションとなる繋ぎの部分が、BT産駒としてはゆってりしていた
kept.note: The quote is word for word (Tomioka). A separate passage on the page says '繋ぎがゆったりとしていることから、脚に掛かる負担が和らげられ、ソエが悪化しなかった', which confirms the pastern trait.

kept.description: His right eye showed white [右目が白い], which made the trainer worry about his temperament. The source does not say whether this means visible white sclera (a folk sign of bad temper) or a pale/wall eye. Candidate for an eye parameter (eye white / eye colour).
kept.quote: 右目が白いから、気が悪くないかと心配してたんです
kept.note: The quote is word for word (Yamauchi). I changed the description from 'his right eye was white' (read as eye colour) to make the ambiguity explicit. Yamauchi links it to temperament, which fits the folklore about visible eye white better than a statement about iris colour. The renderer should not assume a blue eye.

kept.description: Ungainly action in his 2001 Japan Cup drive, with his head pumping violently up and down [激しく頭を上下させ]. Described by one columnist for one race.
kept.quote: 激しく頭を上下させ、前肢を高く振り上げ振り下ろす。どちらかといえば不格好と言えるかもしれないフォームで
kept.note: The quote is word for word in the uma-furi column (Takahashi Kaoru, 2023) on the 2001 Japan Cup. No other fetched source mentions his racing form: Japanese Wikipedia, the netkeiba 名馬列伝, the JRA-VAN memorial, and Number 850824 (pages 1-3) and 838161 were all searched. I lowered the value from 1.4 to 1.3, because one fan column on one race does not justify a value near the top of the scale.

kept.description: In the same Japan Cup drive he flung his forelegs high and drove them down [前肢を高く振り上げ振り下ろす]. The writer calls it a somewhat ungainly form. Single-source observation.
kept.quote: 前肢を高く振り上げ振り下ろす。どちらかといえば不格好と言えるかもしれないフォーム
kept.note: The quote is word for word, but it is the same single fan column on a single race, and no corroboration was found. I lowered the value from 1.25 to 1.15 to match how thin the evidence is.

kept.description: Ran with his tongue hanging out [舌を出しながら走る仕草]; in the Derby he crossed the line with his tongue out. The same writer lists his post-win roars and his habit of idling once in front. Candidate for a 'tongue out' parameter.
kept.quote: 勝利後の雄叫びや、舌を出しながら走る仕草。先頭に立つと遊んでしまうところなど
kept.note: The quote is word for word. The same column also says he finished the 2001 Derby '舌を出す余裕も見せながら1着でゴールイン', so the writer presents it as a recurring personal trait.

kept.description: Tossed his head hard and 'roared' after wins: he violently nodded his head on the Derby winning lap and threw his head up with mouth open after the Japan Cup [激しく頭を上下させる / 天高く吠えた]. Post-race behaviour; candidate for a head-toss parameter.
kept.quote: ウイニングランの場面では大歓声のなか、激しく頭を上下させる姿が見られた。 / ジャングルポケットも頭を上げて激しく口を割って天高く吠えた。
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジャングルポケット_(競走馬)
kept.note: Both quotes are word for word: the first is the Japanese Wikipedia line on the Derby winning lap, the second is the uma-furi line on the Japan Cup. The uma-furi column describes the same roar after the Derby too ('激しく口を割って天高く吠えた。一度、二度。').

kept.description: Did not always run straight once let go. In the Kyodo Tsushin Hai he dived sharply inward and fought the rein with his head up, looking toward the stands [ヨレる / 真っ直ぐ走らず]. Candidate for a 'drift/lug' parameter.
kept.quote: 直線では楽な手応えで抜け出し、ゴール前でヨレるそぶりを見せながらも完勝。 / 一気に内側へ大きく切れ込んだ。…頭を上げてそれに抵抗するジャングルポケットはスタンドへ顔を向けながら走った。真っ直ぐ走らずに
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジャングルポケット_(競走馬)
kept.note: Both quotes are word for word, and the uma-furi column confirms the race was the 2001 Kyodo Tsushin Hai, his first Tokyo start. It is documented for one race only, so a mild drift setting would fit better than a strong one.

kept.description: Hooves 'thin and flat like a plate' [蹄は皿のように薄くて平べったく]; the poor feet troubled his connections at four. This is hoof shape rather than size, so it is a candidate for a hoof-shape parameter.
kept.quote: マンハッタンカフェの蹄は皿のように薄くて平べったく、それが4歳になった頃状態が悪化。
kept.note: The quote is word for word, under Japanese Wikipedia's 特徴 > 蹄の不安 section. The page also describes hoof trouble before the 2002 Nikkei Sho. Leaving param null is correct, because 'flat and thin' describes shape and quality, not size.

kept.description: A tall horse: 170 cm at the withers (16.3 hands) [体高：170cm]. Overall height; no listed parameter covers it.
kept.quote: 体高：170cm / Manhattan Cafe was a black horse standing 16.3 hands (1.70 metres)
kept.note: Both figures appear word for word: '体高：170cm' on the JRHA Stallions in Japan page (青鹿毛 1998年生) and '16.3 hands (1.70 metres)' on English Wikipedia. I did not re-fetch the JRHA PDF, so I dropped it from the sources; the two fetched pages are enough.

kept.description: Thin, weak hoof walls from birth that cracked with racing [生まれつき蹄が薄く / 蹄が弱く]. Close relatives shared the trait, and he was shod with resin (Equilox) and nail-free shoes. Hoof quality, not size: candidate for a hoof-shape/quality parameter.
kept.quote: 生まれつき蹄が薄く、レースを使いこんでいくと亀裂を生じやすかった。デュランダルの近親に共通する特徴でもあった。 / デュランダルは生まれつき蹄が弱く
kept.note: Both quotes are word for word: the netkeiba column '聖剣の勇者(デュランダル)' (2014) and Japanese Wikipedia. Wikipedia describes covering the hoof with エクイロックス resin and then fitting the shoe '釘を使わずに' (without nails); I changed 'glue-on shoes' to 'nail-free shoes' to match.

kept.description: Imposing, well-developed upper body (trunk) typical of Danehill progeny, combined with immature legs [立派な上体と、脚元の未熟さ]. The source says 'upper body' generally and calls it a sire-line trait, so only a slight chest boost is justified.
kept.quote: デインヒル産駒の特徴である立派な上体と、脚元の未熟さを兼ね備えていたため
kept.note: The quote is word for word on the page for the real mare. '立派な上体' means a generally well-developed trunk, framed as a typical Danehill trait; it says nothing specifically about chest width. I lowered the value from 1.06 to 1.03 so the mapping does not overclaim.

kept.description: Over-keen in her races: she pulled hard and was hard to control from the 2002 Arima Kinen onward [行きっぷりが良すぎる / かかってしまい / 制御不可能]. Candidate for a 'pulling/fighting the rider' parameter.
kept.quote: 以前から行きっぷりが良すぎる面もあったファインモーションだが / スタートから先行したがかかってしまい / 制御不可能となり直線で全く伸びず9着に敗退
kept.note: All three fragments are word for word: the first on the JRA-VAN memorial, the other two on Japanese Wikipedia (2002 Arima Kinen and 2004 Mile CS). JRA-VAN says it affected her races more often after that Arima Kinen.

kept.description: Won the 2003 Tenno Sho (Spring) 'with a stride even more powerful than in the Kikuka Sho' [力強いストライド]. This is a race-report phrase, not a documented gait trait: no source describes his strides as long or his action as unusual.
kept.quote: 菊花賞以上に力強いストライドで２つ目のＧＩタイトルを獲得した。
kept.note: The quote is word for word on the JRA-VAN memorial for the real horse. It praises power in one race and says nothing about stride length, so stride 1.05 was not a fair reading. Japanese Wikipedia and both uma-furi columns contain no ストライド/フォーム/走法/跳び description. I removed the parameter (now null); keep this as flavour text or drop it, but do not use it to drive the model.

kept.description: A very big, imposing black horse: 540 kg at his debut, towering over his rivals. When inspecting him as a youngster in the US, Fujisawa called him 'black and huge' [黒くてでっかくて / 雄大な黒鹿毛]. Overall size; no listed parameter covers it.
kept.quote: 新馬戦の馬体重は540キロと、ひと際目を引く雄大な黒鹿毛は、ほかの出走馬を見下ろしているようにさえ感じられた。 / 黒くてでっかくて見栄えがする。
kept.note: Both quotes are word for word. On Japanese Wikipedia, Fujisawa's remark comes from his inspection visit to America before the failed sale, not from the adult horse; I clarified that timing in the description. The 540 kg debut weight supports the size claim.

kept.description: As a three-month-old foal he looked long-legged and gangly [脚の長い、ひょろっとした馬]. Candidate for a leg-length parameter. This describes him as a foal, so it applies to the adult only loosely.
kept.quote: 脚の長い、ひょろっとした馬だな
kept.note: The quote is word for word (owner-breeder Wada Takahiro, about the 3-month-old foal). The foal-only caveat in the description is accurate.

kept.description: Wandered and drifted in the straight on right-handed tracks: he lugged in and wavered in the Arima Kinen and veered both ways in the 2003 Takarazuka Kinen, so Fujisawa concluded he disliked right-handed courses [内へヨレる / フラフラ / 内外に斜行]. Candidate for a 'drift/lug' parameter.
kept.quote: 最後の直線で内へヨレる素振りを見せた / 有馬記念・宝塚記念にてフラフラしたことから、右回りが苦手であると推察し / 直線で内外に斜行したことが原因とも述懐している
kept.note: All three fragments are word for word on Japanese Wikipedia. Peslier also says he was 'モノ見をしていた' in the 2002 Arima Kinen straight. Wikipedia adds that training on left-handed work made him forget the right-handed habit, so this is a right-handed-course tendency rather than a constant trait.

kept.description: Her trainer, Mitsuru Hashida, said that when she got upset her eyes went bloodshot red in an instant. She was walking back on the horse path outside Ritto's E course and was startled by a workout on the inner track. He had never seen a horse whose eye colour changed that fast. He called her extremely high-strung, the most hypersensitive horse he ever handled (一瞬で目が真っ赤になった / 一番過敏な馬). This is a passing, excitement-driven change to the eyes, not a build trait. It could become a new 'agitated eye' visual parameter.
kept.quote: その時、一瞬で目が真っ赤になったんです。一気に血圧が上がるのでしょうね。あんな一瞬で目の色が変わる馬は見たことがなかったです。
kept.note: WebFetch was blocked, so the page was re-fetched with curl. It is a Nikkan Sports column (2022-07-08) by trainer Mitsuru Hashida about the real Admire Groove. The quote is there word for word, and so is '私が扱った中で、一番過敏な馬でした'. param null is right, because this is a temporary state, not anatomy.

kept.description: Mirco Demuro said that in the Satsuki Sho stretch duel with Sakura President, Neo Universe had his ears pinned flat back (耳を絞って). He described him as a horse who loved fighting other horses and tried harder the closer a rival came.
kept.quote: 馬が近くにくればくるほど、もっと頑張れる馬でした。あのときも耳を絞ってすごかったなぁ。
kept.note: Re-fetched. It is a netkeiba column with Demuro about the real Neo Universe, describing the Satsuki Sho finish against Sakura President, and the quote is there word for word. 'あのときも' ('that time too') suggests he did this habitually in duels. 0.8 (mostly pinned) is a fair reading, though the ears may only go back fully when a rival is alongside.

kept.description: Teruya Yoshida (Shadai Farm) said Neo Universe's hocks were deeply angled (飛節の折りが深い). He called this a Sunday Silence trait. He said it after the Derby, explaining why the late-born foal (May 21) had looked unimpressive. No current parameter covers hock angle, so this is a candidate for a new hind-leg angle parameter.
kept.quote: 成長が遅れていたわけだし、飛節の折りが深くて、やや腰が甘い感じに見えるのも、サンデーサイレンスそっくりの特徴だった
kept.note: The quote is in the article, said by 吉田照哉 (Teruya Yoshida), and I added the clause before it for context. I removed 'giving a sickle-hocked look'. 飛節の折りが深い means deeply angled hocks. The source does not call this the sickle-hock fault, so the claim overstated it. param stays null.

kept.description: In the same remark, Yoshida said he looked slightly soft through the loins and hindquarters (やや腰が甘い感じに見える), like Sunday Silence. He was describing how the late foal looked while still growing. As a foal Yoshida also called him long-legged and gangly (脚長でひょろりとした). At most this means very slightly light quarters.
kept.quote: 飛節の折りが深くて、やや腰が甘い感じに見えるのも、サンデーサイレンスそっくりの特徴だった / 幼駒の頃は馬体の形こそ良かったものの、脚長でひょろりとした頼りない姿であったという
kept.note: Both quotes are on the page, attributed to 吉田照哉. In context the remark explains how he looked as a young, late-maturing horse ('成長が遅れていたわけだし'), and the trait is only 'やや' (slight) and 'look'. So I eased the value from 0.96 to 0.97 and made the description say the comment is about how he looked while young.

kept.description: He repeatedly drifted or lugged while finishing in the stretch. In the 2003 Aoba Sho he drifted outward (外側に斜行) and bumped Kraftwerk before he was straightened. In the 2004 autumn Tenno Sho he leaned in (もたれた) until the jockey's left-handed whip straightened him. In the 2005 autumn Tenno Sho he made his run while hanging inward (内にもたれながら). In the 2004 Takarazuka Kinen he also finished tired and drifting (余力なく斜行). This could become a new 'drift/lug' run parameter.
kept.quote: もたれたが左ステッキが入って持ち直し、もう一伸びして差し切った。／抵抗するダンスインザムードと並び立ったが、内にもたれながらの進出だった。／半ば過ぎには、ゼンノロブロイが外側に斜行している。
kept.note: I checked the raw wikitext. All three sentences are there word for word, in the paragraphs for the 2003 Aoba Sho (the 5月3日 青葉賞 paragraph, filed under the 東京優駿 heading), the 2004 autumn Tenno Sho and the 2005 autumn Tenno Sho, so the race attribution is right. I added the 2004 Takarazuka Kinen line ('余力なく斜行しながらの終いとなり') as one more example. param null is right.

kept.description: Her eyes were 'sanpaku' (三白眼): white sclera showed around the iris, the same as her damsire Dancing Brave. This is an eye feature with no current parameter.
kept.quote: 中でも3番仔の目は、末脚の鋭さで鳴らした母父ダンシングブレーヴと同じ三白眼だった。
kept.note: Re-fetched. The page is about the real racehorse, and the '3番仔' (third foal) is Sweep Tosho herself, as the next sentence gives her the name. The quote is there word for word. It is a candidate for a new eye-white parameter.

kept.description: Carrot Farm's Kazuki Nagashima described her as having a muscular body that would put a colt to shame (牡馬顔負けの筋肉質な馬体). This is a statement about her whole body. It is mapped to slightly heavier, more muscled quarters as the nearest parameter.
kept.quote: シーザリオの素晴らしさは、牡馬顔負けの筋肉質な馬体と、最後の勝負根性を生む猛々しい気性。
kept.note: Page 1 of the Sportiva article (curl) contains 'キャロットファームの永島一樹氏が語る。「シーザリオの素晴らしさは、牡馬顔負けの筋肉質な馬体と、最後の勝負根性' (the rest is on page 2). Japanese Wikipedia has the full sentence. The quote is about the real Cesario, the dam of Epiphaneia. The source does not single out the hindquarters, so the mapping is an interpretation, but 1.06 is a modest value and not exaggerated.

kept.description: She was a big, heavy filly. She won the Oaks at 484 kg (馬体重484kg), the second-heaviest Oaks winner after Tesco Gaby (486 kg). Her dam, Takano Secretary, was also large, taking after Seattle Slew. No overall body-size parameter exists.
kept.quote: 馬体重484kgでの優勝はテスコガビーの486kgに次ぐ史上2番目だった。
kept.note: The quote is in the raw wikitext word for word. The dam's size is backed by 'タカノセクレタリーはシアトルスルーの傾向を強く受け継いで体が大きかった'. It is a candidate for a new overall size or scale parameter. param null is right, since spreading it across chest and quarters values would be guesswork.

kept.description: She raced in a hood (覆面) from her second start, the Kunshiran Sho, because she was sensitive to sound. This is equipment, not anatomy, but it matters if the model draws race-day hoods.
kept.quote: 音に敏感だったため、覆面を装着するようになっていた。
kept.note: The quote is in the wikitext paragraph for the 3月26日 君子蘭賞 (500万円以下), which was her second start, right after her debut maiden race. So 'from her second start' is correct.

kept.description: Her only jockey, Katsumi Ando, who rode her in every race, said her action was light and supple, the opposite of her heavy-moving half-brother Daiwa Major (same dam, different sire). He called her light in a good way [良い意味で軽い感じ], supple [しなやか] and very nimble [凄く軽快な馬]. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for a 'springiness / suppleness' parameter.
kept.quote: メジャーはさっき話したように、重量感のあるタイプだったけど、反対に、スカーレットの方は良い意味で軽い感じ。
kept.note: The live keibalab page refused connections, so I checked the Wayback copy of the same URL (title: 安藤勝己騎手×諸星由美(前編)). All three phrases are there and are said about Scarlet: 「スカーレットの方は良い意味で軽い感じ」, 「“しなやか”だから」 and 「もともと凄く軽快な馬だから」. Japanese Wikipedia confirms that Ando rode her in every race (主戦騎手は安藤勝己で、全戦に騎乗した).

kept.description: A very small, slight horse [体型は小柄]. He won the Asahi Hai FS at 416 kg and the Takarazuka Kinen at 424 kg, both the lightest winners in each race's history. He also won the Arima Kinen at 426 kg, the lightest winner since graded races began. As a foal he was slight [華奢な体つき] and by far the smallest of his crop [同期生のなかでは群を抜いて小さかった]. At stud, his small body [小柄な体] is still noted. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for an overall body-scale parameter.
kept.quote: 体型は小柄で、直線で鋭い脚を使う馬であり
kept.note: The weights were wrong. Wikipedia gives the Takarazuka Kinen weight as 424 kg (朝日杯FSの416kg、宝塚記念の424kgもレース史上最少体重優勝記録). The 426 kg figure was his Arima Kinen, the lightest winner since graded races began. All the other quotes are confirmed: 「小柄」 is in Wikipedia; 「華奢な体つき」 and 「群を抜いて小さかった」 are in Yushun; 「小さな体で57キロを背負った」 is in uma-furusato.

kept.description: Described as having a large, imposing frame [雄大な馬体], with a build in no way inferior to the JRA horses [決して体つきは中央の馬たちにも劣らない]. The only source is a fan essay on uma-furi, so confidence is low. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for an overall body-scale parameter.
kept.quote: 雄大な馬体と少し濃いめの栗毛の馬体に、チェック模様のメンコ。
kept.note: The quote is confirmed, and the page is about the real Furioso (Brian's Time, bred at Hashimoto Farm). The source says his build was 'not inferior' to the JRA horses (劣らない), not 'no smaller', so I corrected the description. It is a fan essay (それぞれの競馬愛, by an ウマフリライター). The Japanese Wikipedia source has no body descriptors, so nothing corroborates it.

kept.description: A stride runner with a big, long stride. Nishiyama, manager of her breeder Country Bokujo, said her stride was big [跳び（１完歩）が大きく]. Fujii, the farm's training lead, said they taught her how to use her neck [首の使い方を教え込んだ]. Yushun describes her as having a long-striding action [ストライドの大きな走り]. SPAIA describes her clean, sweeping footwork [跳びのきれいな…雄大なフットワーク] in the Hanshin JF, against Aston Machan's pitch running.
kept.quote: 跳び（１完歩）が大きく、ゴール手前では無駄なく真直ぐに走って
kept.note: All three quotes are on the pages, and each page is about Vodka: 「ストライドの大きな走りは東京の２４００㍍に向いている」 (Yushun) and 「跳びのきれいな黒鹿毛が…雄大なフットワークで」 (SPAIA, contrasted with 「アストンマーチャンがピッチ走法で」). With three independent sources, 1.08 is a fair value.

kept.description: An asymmetric hind action. Trainer Katsuhiko Sumii said she twisted her right hind leg as she brought it forward [右トモをひねりながら前に出していた]. Energy leaked out through that twist, so she could not run at full power on right-handed tracks. That may explain her record at left-handed Tokyo, and he linked it to her heel trouble. Wikipedia, citing Yushun (Nov 2009), says she had overcome it by the autumn of her 5-year-old season. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for a hind-leg twist or left/right asymmetry parameter.
kept.quote: 右トモをひねって走る癖があり、そこからエネルギーが抜けてしまうことに起因しているのではないか
kept.note: The netkeiba column, by Akihiro Shimada, has the quote word for word, reporting what Sumii said. Wikipedia has Sumii's direct quote 「右トモをひねりながら前に出していたんです。そこからエネルギーが逃げるので右回りだと力を出し切れず…」 and adds 「5歳秋時点ではそれを克服していた」, citing 『優駿』2009年11月号. The netkeiba column does not mention that it was overcome, so that point rests on Wikipedia/Yushun.

kept.description: A tall, large-framed horse. When he arrived at stud, breeders called him tall with a striking body [背が高く、すごい馬体だ]. A photo caption describes a large frame that still did not look heavy [雄大だが重苦しさを感じさせない馬体]. He was so well balanced that he did not look like a 500 kg horse [バランスが良いから500キロには見えない]. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for an overall height/scale parameter.
kept.quote: 背が高く、すごい馬体だ
kept.note: The page covers Espoir City's arrival at Yushun Stallion Station. All three phrases are there: 「背が高く、すごい馬体だ」, 「雄大だが重苦しさを感じさせない馬体」 (photo caption) and 「バランスが良いから500キロには見えない」. It is a single stud-arrival report, so confidence stays moderate.

kept.description: A narrow, slab-sided body. JRDB's conformation reviews call her thin-bodied like her dam Biwa Heidi [薄身の体つき] (Tulip Sho) and thin-bodied and slightly croup-high [薄身のやや腰高体型] (Oka Sho).
kept.quote: 母ビワハイジ同様、薄身の体つきだけに、馬体全体からのインパクトには欠ける
kept.note: I fetched both pages over HTTP; the HTTPS certificate has expired. 51137223 is the JRDB 血統＆馬体講座 for Buena Vista at the Tulip Sho and contains the exact quote. 51155916 (Oka Sho) says 「馬体は母父カーリアンよりで薄身のやや腰高体型」. 0.93 is a fair value for 薄身.

kept.description: Fine-boned. Three JRDB reviews describe her as a fine-boned speed type [骨が細めのスピードタイプ], with fine bone and a sharp build [骨が細くてシャープな体つき] and slightly slim cannons [やや細めの管（芝向き）].
kept.quote: 骨が細めのスピードタイプで、体つきに比べて繋が長く
kept.note: The wording is consistent across three races: 51137223 (Tulip Sho), 「骨が細めのスピードタイプ」; 51172013 (Yushun Himba), 「骨が細くてシャープな体つき」; and 51088907 (Hanshin JF), 「やや細めの管（芝向き）」.

kept.description: Small overall. Yushun's 2016 retrospective on her racing career calls her small and quiet [小柄でおとなしく]. However, JRDB's Yushun Himba review says she stood tall for her weight and did not look especially small [馬体重の割に体高があり、さほど小さくは見えない], and she raced at about 446-450 kg at age 2-3. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for an overall body-scale parameter.
kept.quote: 小柄でおとなしく
kept.note: The quote is confirmed in Yushun (story13/653, by 軍土門隼夫), but it is a writer's general characterization. JRDB's own wording, 「さほど小さくは見えない」, partly contradicts it, and JRDB lists her at 446-450 kg. I rewrote the description to include that counterpoint and to make clear the 'small' reading is modest.

kept.description: In the 2008 Hanshin JF she moved up with a relaxed action that made good use of her neck [首を使ったゆったりした走り]. This is a single-race observation.
kept.quote: 後方に位置すると、首を使ったゆったりした走りで徐々に進出を開始。
kept.note: The quote is exact in the Hanshin JF race comment (51088907). Because it comes from a single race, the mild 1.1 is appropriate.

kept.description: A slender build for a colt. JRDB described him at his debut as slim [細身の腰高] and later as compact [コンパクトな体つき; 体重も体高もそれほどなく]. His stud farm said he had looked slight for a colt while racing [牡馬としては線の細い印象だった馬体] and had filled out at stud. Barrel is the closest parameter, but this really describes an overall light frame.
kept.quote: 細身の腰高で、スピードを感じさせる馬体をしている。
kept.note: 51055691 is the debut review (新馬戦, 2008-11-02, 450 kg) and contains the exact quote. 51071762 (Tokyo Sports Hai) says 「背中が短く腰高でコンパクトな体つき」 and 「体重も体高もそれほどなく」. The uma-furusato stud column says 「牡馬としては線の細い印象だった馬体も、逞しく、種牡馬らしい体型へと変貌した」. The value is fair for his racing-age look.

kept.description: Croup-high [腰高], meaning his croup stood above his withers. Two JRDB reviews at age 2 say so, the second describing a short back [背中が短く]. This suggests relatively low withers. It was noted only at age 2, when croup-high builds are common.
kept.quote: 背中が短く腰高でコンパクトな体つき。
kept.note: Both quotes are confirmed (「細身の腰高」 at the debut and 「背中が短く腰高」 at the Tokyo Sports Hai). Reading 腰高 as somewhat low withers is a reasonable proxy, and -0.3 is modest. Both observations are from age 2 only.

kept.description: Hind legs trailing out behind instead of stepping well under [トモ（後肢）が流れる]. JRDB noted this twice at age 2 and saw it as a juvenile weakness. The second review says it was slight and not a concern [若干流れる面はあるものの、気になるほどではなく]. There is no evidence it lasted.
kept.quote: 現状では腰の甘さが目につき、トモ（後肢）が流れていた。
kept.note: The quote is exact. However, the second review (51071762) is a paddock/walking note ('非常に姿勢が良くしっかり歩いている') and says 「トモ（後肢）が若干流れる面はあるものの、気になるほどではなく」. That is a transient juvenile trait, slight by the second race, in a horse who later won the Takarazuka Kinen. I softened hindDrive from 0.93 to 0.96.

kept.description: Long-limbed. JRDB said at her debut that her legs were a little longer than standard [手脚は標準よりも少し長く], and at the Oka Sho that her legs were long [手脚も長め]. Her yearling syndicate catalog predicted she would develop a long-legged, tall frame like her sire Manhattan Cafe [脚長で体高のある馬体]. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for a leg-length parameter.
kept.quote: 手脚は標準よりも少し長く、繋も少し長め。
kept.note: The debut review (51101847, 2009-01-04, 476 kg) contains the exact quote. The Oka Sho page (51155916) has 「手脚も長め」 in the Red Desire section. The umadb catalog page is about the right horse (Manhattan Cafe x Great Sunrise) and says 「父マンハッタンカフェに似た、脚長で体高のある馬体に変わっていくかと思われます」, which is a prediction.

kept.description: At her debut she ran with her upper body carried slightly high [若干、上体が高い走法].
kept.quote: 若干、上体が高い走法で、やや重心を右に傾けて走っていた。
kept.note: The quote is exact in the debut race comment. 上体 (forehand/upper body) maps loosely to headCarriage, and 若干 justifies the small value of 0.3. It is a single-race observation.

kept.description: At her debut she ran leaning her weight slightly to the right [やや重心を右に傾けて]. This is a single-race observation. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for a lateral-lean parameter.
kept.quote: やや重心を右に傾けて走っていた
kept.note: The quote is exact, in the same debut race comment. It comes from one race only.

kept.description: A roomy belly [腹袋も大きく] and a slightly long body, according to JRDB's Oka Sho note. Its debut review instead called her medium-built and well balanced [前後躯のバランスが取れた中肉中背], so confidence is low.
kept.quote: やや胴が長く、腹袋も大きく、手脚も長めと距離が伸びてこそ能力発揮できる体付き。
kept.note: The quote is exact in the Red Desire section of the Oka Sho page (she finished 2nd). The debut page does say 「前後躯のバランスが取れた中肉中背」, so the low confidence stated in the claim is correct. 1.05 is mild.

kept.description: Fine-boned. In JRDB's Hopeful Stakes review (age 2) his bone is described as rather fine [骨も細め], giving a slim, rangy look.
kept.quote: 四肢が長く骨も細めなのでかなりスラリとした見映え。
kept.note: The page is the JRDB Hopeful S review of Tosen Jordan (Jungle Pocket x Every Whisper, 470 kg, 2008-12-28), and the quote is exact. It is a single source at age 2.

kept.description: Long legs and a rangy, slim outline [四肢が長く…スラリとした見映え]. None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for a leg-length parameter.
kept.quote: 四肢が長く骨も細めなのでかなりスラリとした見映え。
kept.note: The quote is exact, in the same review.

kept.description: He ran with a scooping foreleg action [前肢を掻き込んで走る] but a very supple stride [非常にしなやかなストライド]. JRDB, Hopeful Stakes race comment, age 2.
kept.quote: 前肢を掻き込んで走るが非常にしなやかなストライドで、長く脚を使えて勢いにも乗れる。
kept.note: The quote is exact, and the vocabulary maps 掻き込み to higher kneeAction, so 1.12 stays. I removed 'rolling' from the description because the source does not say it. It is a single-race observation at age 2.

kept.description: A high-set, high-carried neck [首の高い馬]. Writer Takayuki Jiromaru (blog 'Glass no Keibajo') says this while noting that Transcend's son Engrosseur inherited it, in the context of running action: a high-necked horse struggles to use a long finishing kick. headCarriage is the closest parameter.
kept.quote: 父のトランセンドも首の高い馬でしたので、その点は父譲りかと思います。
kept.note: The quote is exact. The surrounding text, 「首の高い馬は、長い脚を使うことが難しいため」, shows that it refers to running action, which supports mapping it to headCarriage. It is a single source and an aside about another horse, so 0.4 is moderate and fair.

kept.description: A big horse of over 500 kg [500キロを超える大型馬]. He weighed 534 kg in the post-workout weigh-in announced on 14 February ahead of the 2013 February Stakes, against 518 kg at his previous race. His weight was also known to swing by double digits from race to race (+14, -10, +12 kg). None of the parameters covers this. It is a candidate for an overall body-scale parameter.
kept.quote: 馬体重が500キロを超える大型馬ではあったが
kept.note: The quote is in the real-horse (史実) episode section of a GameWith Uma Musume guide page. It is a secondary, game-site source, but it is explicitly about the real horse. Radio Nikkei lists 「ワンダーアキュート ５３４ ２／１４ 栗東 ５１８」 in a table of post-workout (調教後) weights for the 30th February Stakes. That is not a race-day declared weight, so I corrected the description. The JRDB debut review records 496 kg.

kept.description: A solid frame with a big, roomy belly, a typical dirt horse [骨格がしっかりしていて腹袋が大きく]. JRDB, debut review.
kept.quote: 骨格がしっかりしていて腹袋が大きく、いかにもダート馬といった感じ。
kept.note: The page is the JRDB debut review of Wonder Acute (Charismatic x Wonder Heritage, Kyoto dirt 1800, 2009-01-24, 496 kg), and the quote is exact. It is a single source, so confidence is moderate.

kept.description: At his debut his hind legs did not step far under the body [後肢の踏み込みも少し甘い], and his joints were a little loose. This comes from a single early conformation review.
kept.quote: 四肢の関節は少し緩く、後肢の踏み込みも少し甘い。
kept.note: The quote is exact, but it is a single debut conformation note that says 'slightly' (少し). He later won G1 dirt races, so I softened hindDrive from 0.93 to 0.96 to avoid overstating a juvenile, one-off observation.

kept.description: Known for a jet-black, glossy coat and a handsome, well-featured face [漆黒の艶やかな馬体と端正な顔立ち]. This is about looks (coat sheen and facial refinement). No source gives a head size, so no head value is set.
kept.quote: 漆黒の艶やかな馬体と端正な顔立ちでも人気だったダービー馬は、悠然とした雰囲気で馬運車から降り立ち
kept.note: Re-fetched the Sanspo article (31 Oct 2025, about the real Derby winner retiring to Versailles Resort Farm); the quote is there word for word. The ja.wikipedia 現役時 line says the same: 漆黒の艶やかな馬体と端正な顔立ちなど. Leaving param null is right, because neither source gives a head size.

kept.description: Habitually slow away from the gate [出遅れ癖]. In the 2012 Japan Cup he tried to duck under the gate [ゲートをもぐろうとし]. In the 2012 Arima Kinen he reared up in the stall as it opened [ゲート内で立ち上がってしまい] and lost about 10 lengths. His trainer called it 'severe' [重症です]. This is gate behaviour; no build or running parameter fits.
kept.quote: 前走のジャパンカップでもゲートをもぐろうとし、スタートが遅れて３着に甘んじており、角居勝彦調教師も「なかなか直せない。重症です」 / スタートと同時にゲート内で立ち上がってしまい、10馬身近い歴史的な大出遅れとなった
kept.note: The first quote is word for word in the Sponichi article of 23 Dec 2012, written after the Arima Kinen. The second is word for word in the ja.wikipedia race narrative. Sportiva (2025) adds: 現役時代は、出遅れ癖がある馬として知られていた, and the race-call figure of about 10 lengths. All three pages are about the real horse. Param null is right.

kept.description: A big horse with a long, bounding stride [大型で跳びの大きい走法]. He was still handy enough to win four graded races on Nakayama's tight turns, which big-striding horses usually find hard. The Japanese article's 特徴 section cites Shukan Keiba Book, 26 Dec 2010, p.15.
kept.quote: 大型で跳びの大きい走法だが、上手く流れに乗る器用さがある
kept.note: Word for word in the ja.wikipedia 特徴 section, with ref 『週刊競馬ブック』2010年12月26日号、p.15. The next sentence frames him as a 大跳び horse (一般的に大跳びの馬が苦にするとされる小回りの中山競馬場で重賞を4勝). 大跳び is the vocabulary's anchor for 1.1, so the value is a fair reading.

kept.description: On good turf he ran with a pitch-oriented action [ピッチを重視する走り方], meaning quicker, shorter strides. In the Derby on heavy ground he kept a long stride [ストライドが長い状態を保ったまま]. This comes from a JRA Equine Research Institute column by Takahashi Toshiyuki.
kept.quote: オルフェーヴル号は、芝馬場の良の状態では、ピッチを重視する走り方をしていたが、不良馬場で行われたダービーでは、ストライドが長い状態を保ったまま走っていた。
kept.note: Downloaded and read the JRA PDF (サラブレッドのスポーツ科学 第60回, JRA競走馬総合研究所 高橋敏之, p.17); the sentence is word for word. ja.wikipedia quotes it too. 0.95 is a mild pitch lean for good ground, which is his normal racing surface, so it is fair and not exaggerated.

kept.description: Jockey Ikezoe said that when asked for speed he 'sank' as he took hold of the bit [沈むようにハミを取って], lowering himself as he accelerated (2011 Arima Kinen). This is one jockey's impression of how he quickened, not a description of his whole-race form.
kept.quote: (勝負どころの) スピード の乗りは抜群で、ちょっと仕掛けたら沈むようにハミを取って進んでいってくれて、ねじ伏せるように直線伸びてくれた。
kept.note: The quote is word for word in netkeiba news 60772 (Ikezoe, Arima Kinen, 25 Dec 2011). ja.wikipedia gives a variant: スピードの乗りは抜群で沈むように走りました. I lowered bodyLow from 0.5 to 0.3. The source is a single rider's figurative remark about how he lowered while accelerating when asked. It does not describe a habitually low whole-body form, so mid-scale over-reads it.

kept.description: Habitually drifted and hung in once in front [斜行癖 / 内にもたれる]. He cut to the inside rail in his debut, and in the 2012 Arc he veered sharply to the inside rail after taking the lead. Candidate for a new 'drift/lug-in' parameter.
kept.quote: 凱旋門賞敗退の原因にもなった斜行癖を矯正するために、1頭でもヨレずに走らせるような工夫が施された / スミヨンは「直線に向いてから追い出しての反応は良かったが、内にもたれてしまった。」
kept.note: Both phrases are in ja.wikipedia. The 斜行癖 sentence is in the 2013 training narrative and the Soumillon quote is in the 2012 Arc section. The same page supports the debut detail (最終的に内ラチまで切れ込み) and the Arc detail (内ラチに向かって急激に斜行して失速). Param null is right.

kept.description: Bolted mid-race [逸走]. In the 2012 Hanshin Daishoten he refused to take the third turn and ran straight out to the outside rail, then rejoined and finished second. He also threw his jockey after the line in his debut and in the Kikuka Sho. Behaviour quirk, not a build parameter.
kept.quote: 1頭になり競馬を止めようとしたオルフェーヴルは、2周目の第3コーナー入口でコーナーを曲がろうとせずに外ラチギリギリの所まで真っ直ぐに逸走し始め
kept.note: Word for word in the ja.wikipedia 阪神大賞典 (2012) section. The same page has the throws: ゴール後には池添を振り落として放馬 in the debut, and in the Kikuka Sho 外ラチに向かって逸走しデビュー戦同様に池添を振り落とす. The 2nd-place finish (半馬身差...2着敗戦) is also there.

kept.description: A large, long-legged but thin-bodied build [脚長の体型 / 大型馬だけど薄手]. He raced at about 510-522 kg. The interviewer remarked that big horses rarely make stayers, and assistant trainer Nakayama Giichi replied that this one was big but 薄手 (narrow, light through the body), which is why he could handle distance. The long legs and large size have no parameter; the thinness maps to a slightly slab-sided barrel.
kept.quote: 脚長の体型で体も成長してきていますし、しっかり通常通りの調教を積んでのプラス体重なら成長分と受け取って貰っても結構です。 / ただ、この馬は大型馬だけど薄手なので、距離をこなすのではないかと思います
kept.note: Re-fetched the keibalab interview with assistant trainer 中山義一 (今年も打倒オルフェ！ウインバリアシオン); the 脚長 quote is word for word. The 'unusual for a stayer' point comes from the interviewer's question (最近の競馬で大型馬の長距離馬は珍しいように思います). The same answer says 大型馬だけど薄手, which the claim left out. I added it and changed param from null to barrel 0.95, a mild slab-sided reading of 薄手. Leg length and overall size are still unmodelled, so this stays a candidate for a new parameter.

kept.description: Former jockey Katsumi Ando said the horse's gait [歩様] was already suspect, slightly irregular, from the first time he rode him at three. This is a soundness note; it could only be modelled as a slight unevenness in the gait.
kept.quote: オレが初めて乗った時から歩様は怪しかったくらい。 / his gait had already been irregular since he was a 3-year-old
kept.note: The English sentence is in en.wikipedia. The Japanese line is the title of the cited source, a tweet by Ando (@andokatsumi). ja.wikipedia says the same: すでに3歳の頃から歩様がおかしかったとのこと. The original is a single offhand tweet, so this is weak evidence. Param null is right.

kept.description: Her handlers noted a large chest girth [大きな胸囲] when she began training, which they took as a sign of high cardiopulmonary capacity. The Japanese article cites Yushun, Sept 2021, p.42.
kept.quote: 高い心肺能力を示唆する大きな胸囲を持つなど、非凡な素質を見せた
kept.note: Word for word in ja.wikipedia, with ref 『優駿』2021年9月 p.42. 大きな胸囲 means a large girth. A deep chest is the main contributor to girth, so chestDepth 1.07 (between average and 'very deep') is a fair, unexaggerated reading.

kept.description: Ran with a somewhat high neck carriage [いくらか首が高い走法]. Before the Oaks this raised doubts about whether she would stay 2400 m. The Japanese article cites Ezura Hiroya, 名馬を読む (2017), p.295.
kept.quote: さらにいくらか首が高い走法だったことで2400メートルという距離への不安があった
kept.note: Word for word in ja.wikipedia. The ref ezura295 resolves to 江面弘也『名馬を読む』三賢社 2017, p.295. Because the source says いくらか ('somewhat'), +0.3 on a -1..+1 scale is proportionate.

kept.description: Former trainer Suzuki Yasuhiro called her a lean-muscled, willowy type ['細マッチョ', 柳のようにしなやかな馬体], in contrast to the heavily muscled 'gorimatcho' type of Almond Eye. This is an overall body-type impression; the closest parameter is a lightly tucked-up, lean body.
kept.quote: アーモンドアイやデアリングタクト、リバティアイランドは筋骨隆々の“ゴリマッチョ”、ジェンティルドンナは柳に雪折れなしのことわざを体現したような“細マッチョ”でした。
kept.note: The quote is word for word in the Sponichi 達眼 column of 9 Apr 2024 (written about Regaleira, comparing her to Gentildonna). ja.wikipedia repeats it. I lowered tuckUp from 0.4 to 0.25. The source is a retrospective impression of a slim-but-muscled, supple overall build (流麗なボディーライン). It says nothing specific about the belly line, so only a light lean setting is justified.

kept.description: Strong, soft, elastic muscle let him accelerate with a big stride [大きなストライドで加速できた] up the steep final hills at Nakayama and Hanshin. This is the Japanese article's summary, citing Gallop sources that include an interview with Okada Shigeyuki.
kept.quote: ゴールドシップは強靭で柔らかく収縮力のある筋力を持ち、大きなストライドで加速できた
kept.note: Word for word in the ja.wikipedia 身体面 section, citing Gallop 2015 JRA重賞年鑑 and 週刊Gallop臨時増刊 21世紀の名馬 VOL.1 ゴールドシップ pp.76-77. The Okada interview quoted there also says 全身運動でいいストライドで走り. The sentence is the article's summary rather than a direct Okada quote, which is a minor attribution nuance. 1.08 is fair.

kept.description: Markedly loose, soft hind pasterns [後肢の繋ぎが顕著に緩く]. Because of this he could not turn his legs over fast and was slow to break and to quicken, so he usually raced from the back. He was also said to be built so he could not run with a snap of the lower leg [スナップを利かせて走れないつくり]. Candidate for a new pastern-slope/softness parameter.
kept.quote: ゴールドシップの馬体は後肢の繋ぎが顕著に緩く、高速回転が苦手で、スタート時や勝負所でゴーサインを送られた時もこの緩さが災いして、ダッシュが利かない
kept.note: Present in the ja.wikipedia 身体面 section. In the source a footnote ref sits between 繋ぎ and が; otherwise the text matches. The same section has ゴールドシップはスナップを利かせて走れないつくりをしている (Okada, via Gallop 2015 年鑑) and 後肢の繋ぎの緩さ. Param null is right.

kept.description: Reared in the starting gate. In the 2014 Tenno Sho (Spring) he suddenly stood up and growled after loading. In the 2015 Takarazuka Kinen he reared at his neighbour and again as the gates opened [ゲート内で立ち上がる], losing all chance. He was also chronically slow away [行き足が付かず].
kept.quote: ゲート内でトーホウジャッカルを威嚇するように立ち上がるなどして落ち着きを失い、さらにゲートが開けられた瞬間にも立ち上がってしまった
kept.note: Word for word in the ja.wikipedia 2015 宝塚記念 paragraph. The 2014 天皇賞（春） paragraph says ゲート入り後に突如立ち上がってうなり声をだすほど怒りだし. The 2014 races include いつものように行き足が付かず. All are in the same article.

kept.description: A big horse. He was bred from a 500 kg+ dam and the small sire Stay Gold to get a mid-sized foal, but turned out large [大きく産まれた] and stood out among his age group. There is no overall-size parameter.
kept.quote: 誕生した本馬は想定に反して大きく産まれたとのことである / even when young, Gold Ship was big enough to stand out amongst the other horses his age
kept.note: Both quotes are word for word: ja.wikipedia line 49, with 母ポイントフラッグ 500キログラムを超える大型馬 and 小柄な種馬であるステイゴールド in the same sentence, and the en.wikipedia background section. Param null is right.

kept.description: Equipment: wore blinkers from the 2013 Arima Kinen (when Ryan Moore took over) and added a shadow roll [ブリンカーに加えシャドーロール] from the 2014 Takarazuka Kinen. He kept both on, including for the 2014 Arc, until the 2015 Japan Cup, where he ran bare-faced [素顔] for the first time since the 2013 Arima Kinen.
kept.quote: ブリンカーに加えシャドーロールも着用し臨んだ本レースは、12頭立てと頭数こそ少ないものの
kept.note: The quote is word for word (2014 宝塚記念 paragraph). I corrected the timeline. ja.wikipedia says blinkers were first fitted for the 2013 有馬記念 (更にはブリンカーを着用することとなった). The 2015 Japan Cup was 2013年の有馬記念以来となるブリンカー・シャドーロールを外しての素顔, so he wore the gear well past the Arc, not only 'from the 2014 Takarazuka Kinen through the Arc'.

kept.description: A big-framed horse, over 500 kg [500キロを超える馬格], according to a stud column on his stallion career. There is no overall-size parameter.
kept.quote: 配合牝馬を選ばない血統構成と500キロを超える馬格。
kept.note: Word for word in the uma-furusato column ホッコータルマエを訪ねて～優駿スタリオンステーション. The page is about the real stallion; the stud manager (山崎努マネージャー) is quoted next to the line. Param null is right.

kept.description: After the 2012 Queen Cup, jockey Iwata compared her stride [跳び] to how he imagined Deep Impact's action must feel. This praises the quality of her action. It does not say the stride was long or short, so it gives no value to map.
kept.quote: ディープインパクトには乗ったことはないが、こういう跳びをしているのかなと思った
kept.note: The quote is word for word in netkeiba news 61814 (Queen Cup, Iwata) and in ja.wikipedia. I removed stride 1.05 and set param null. The comparison only says her action resembles what he imagined Deep Impact's to be. It states nothing about stride length, and turning it into a length requires facts about Deep Impact from memory, which the rules forbid.

kept.description: Equipment: after losing to Gentildonna throughout the 2012 fillies' Triple Crown, she raced in a hood [メンコ] marked with a large X [バツ印]. The owner designed it as a jinx against Sunday Racing's silks; in the interview 'that year' refers to 2013, her 4-year-old season. Her dam Haruwa Sweet was famously born without a tail, but that applies to the dam, not Verxina.
kept.quote: あの年からサンデーレーシングの勝負服に対抗してメンコにバツ印をデザインしたんです。
kept.note: Word for word in the Chunichi interview with owner Sasaki Kazuhiro. 'あの年' follows his mention of the 13年のヴィクトリアマイル, so 2013 is a fair reading. ja.wikipedia agrees: 牝馬三冠レースではジェンティルドンナに負け続けていたため、その後は...バツ印をデザインしたメンコを着用していた. The tailless-dam fact is in ja.wikipedia (ハルーワスウィートは、先天的に尾骨がなく). Param null is right.

kept.description: A keen, hard-pulling horse. Japanese Wikipedia says the 2013 Yayoi Sho defeat exposed his problem with settling against an intense forward urge [激しい前進気勢], which his dam Cesario also had. He then fought to go forward in the 2013 Satsuki Sho and the Derby. In the 2014 Japan Cup he pulled the whole way ('so hard he nearly collided on the back straight') but still won by 4 lengths. This is a running behaviour that no current parameter covers. A keenness / fighting-the-bit parameter could cover it.
kept.quote: この敗戦により、母シーザリオも持っていた激しい前進気勢に対する折り合いという課題が顕在化した … 「バックストレートでは衝突しそうなくらい」掛かりっぱなしの追走
kept.note: Both phrases are on the page, but they come from different races. The 前進気勢 sentence follows the 2013 Yayoi Sho defeat, not the Japan Cup. The 掛かりっぱなし sentence is about the 2014 Japan Cup. The page says the dam 'also had' the trait, which is not quite 'inherited'. I replaced 'throughout his career' with the races the page actually documents (Yayoi Sho, Satsuki Sho and Derby in 2013, Japan Cup in 2014).

kept.description: Yuta Kimiya, manager of Northern Farm Tenei, worked with Epiphaneia during his racing career. He said the horse himself had a rugged, stiff quality [ゴツゴツした硬いところ], unlike his more supple offspring. This could support a stiffness/suppleness parameter.
kept.quote: 父自身はゴツゴツした硬いところあったのですが、産駒は柔らかみがあります。
kept.note: The quote is in the netkeiba article. The speaker is Yuta Kimiya (木實谷雄太), Northern Farm Tenei, talking about Epiphaneia as a sire. No parameter fits, so it stays null.

kept.description: Trainer Yasuo Tomomichi passed on Hugh Bowman's view that the wide Tokyo course suited the horse better because of 'his big movement'. This suggests a long, reaching stride.
kept.quote: I talked to Bowman afterward and he felt the Tokyo course suited the horse better, with his big movement.
kept.note: The quote is in Tomomichi's comments for the 2018 Arima Kinen. It is one second-hand remark, so the modest 1.05 is a fair reading.

kept.description: After his 2016 Nakayama Kinen comeback, Sponichi wrote that 'the double classic winner's stride was still intact' [２冠馬のストライドは健在]. This treats his stride as a trademark, but the article does not say the stride was long.
kept.quote: ブランク明けでも２冠馬のストライドは健在だった。
kept.note: The quote is in the Sponichi Nakayama Kinen report. None of the other sources I checked (ja.wikipedia, the umanity analysis, the Hochi archive) say 大跳び, 跳びが大きい or 大きなストライド. Because 'big' is only implied, I lowered the value from 1.05 to 1.03.

kept.description: In the 2015 Satsuki Sho he swerved violently at the 4th corner, from near the rail to the far outside ('as if he warped' [まるでワープしたかのように急激に大外へと斜行]). He hampered three horses, and Mirco Demuro was suspended. Demuro blamed it on Duramente's first right-handed race and the noise of the crowd. It was a one-off, not a habit. A drift/lugging-out parameter could cover it.
kept.quote: それまで最内付近にいたドゥラメンテが、まるでワープしたかのように急激に大外へと斜行してしまったのだ。 / 「４コーナーは困りました。初めての右回りというのもありましたし、たぶんファンの大きな声援で馬が怖がってしまったんだと思います」
kept.note: The swerve and the ワープ quote are confirmed for the right horse. But no fetched source says it happened because he 'did not change leads'; 手前 does not appear on the Yahoo page or on ja.wikipedia. Demuro's own explanation (first right-handed track, crowd noise) replaces it. I added the JRA English Derby preview ('veered away from its inside position') as a source.

kept.description: A big-striding horse. Trainer Hisashi Shimizu judged from his long-striding action [ストライドの大きな走り] that he would suit longer distances from the start. Shimizu also said that even before his debut, the horse's stride made the stable think he was a Grade 1 performer. JRA's English site called him 'the big striding colt'.
kept.quote: それでも清水は、ストライドの大きな走りから、当初から長めの距離のほうがいいと思っていたという。 / Even before his debut, the stride this horse has on him had us thinking he was a Grade 1 performer.
kept.note: All three quotes are on their pages: the netkeiba book chapter 1, Shimizu's 2016 Arima comments, and 'The big striding colt' in the 2015 Derby preview. Three independent sources make 1.07 fair.

kept.description: Tall and long-legged from birth: thin skin, tall, long-legged build [背が高く、脚の長い体型]. Farm staff compared his shape to Dance in the Dark. At his retirement the breeder said he was known for his long legs when he was born. A leg-length/height parameter could cover this.
kept.quote: 皮膚が薄く、背が高く、脚の長い体型。
kept.note: The uma-furusato quote is from Iwakura (Yanagawa Bokujo). 弘子さん made the 'ダンスインザダークっぽい' comparison. Hochi quotes breeder Yanagawa: 「生まれた時は脚が長いことで評判でした」. ja.wikipedia has 脚が長い体形、体高が高く. No parameter fits, so it stays null.

kept.description: A large, heavy horse ('He's a big horse'). He weighed 510 kg at his debut and later 530-540 kg, and he set heaviest-winner records in several G1 races. An overall body-size parameter could cover this.
kept.quote: Kitasan Black is a large Thoroughbred who had weighed up to 540 kg in his racing career. / He’s a big horse.
kept.note: The quotes are confirmed on the English Wikipedia page and in Shimizu's Kikuka Sho comments. ja.wikipedia gives 510 kg at debut, growth to 530 kg, and heaviest-winner records in the Kikuka Sho, Osaka Hai, Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen.

kept.description: Described as rich in bone with a well-balanced body [骨量に富み] even as a foal.
kept.quote: 骨量に富み、バランスの良い馬体の持ち主だった
kept.note: The sentence is in the 牧場時代 section of ja.wikipedia. No cannon circumference is given, so the modest 1.06 is a fair reading.

kept.description: Several sources describe his hindquarters as loose or unfinished [トモに緩さ]. As a youngster his hind legs were not filled out. Even as a 5-year-old G1 winner, his work rider said some looseness remained in the hindquarters, leaving room to grow. This is about firmness and maturity, not the size or mass of the quarters.
kept.quote: 黒岩も「トモ（後肢）に緩さが残るので、成長の余地がある」と語る。
kept.note: The quote is in the Nikkei article (June 2017). uma-furusato also has 「もともと体が大きく、トモに緩さがあった」. But 緩さ means looseness or immaturity, not light quarters, so hindquarters 0.96 is not a fair reading. I removed the parameter (now null).

kept.description: A big, long-limbed colt who could not shorten his stride. Trainer Yasutoshi Ikee: 'big and has long limbs and he's not able to take small steps'. Kenta Inubushi, his trainer at Northern Farm Kuko, also described big footwork [フットワークが大きくて]. This fits a long-striding runner.
kept.quote: This colt is big and has long limbs and he’s not able to take small steps so the interference in the Satsuki Sho homestretch hurt. / フットワークが大きくて乗り味も素晴らしいと、能力の高さを感じさせながらも
kept.note: Both quotes are confirmed: Ikee in the 2016 Derby comments, and Inubushi (Northern Farm Kuko) in the uma-furusato Kisaragi Sho report. 1.07 is fair. I did not re-check the English Wikipedia page, so it is dropped from sources.

kept.description: Trainer Yasutoshi Ikee said that in top gear the horse's centre of gravity 'drops sharply and he runs as if sinking' [重心がグッと下がって沈むような走り]. He said this was missing in the 2017 Tenno Sho (Spring) defeat.
kept.quote: 「トップギアに入れば重心がグッと下がって沈むような走りになる馬が、あの日は終始、沈まないままでした。」
kept.note: The quote is on Number page 4/4. The text attributes it to Ikee (「その言葉は池江が贈る最大級の賛辞」). 0.55 is a fair reading of a trait that shows at top speed.

kept.description: A very small mare. She mostly raced at 410-419 kg up to age 3 and never weighed more than 440 kg [小柄な馬体]. Her 414 kg is the lightest of any Shuka Sho winner. Her trainer said 'her body is still small'. Farm staff saw her as a smaller version of her full sister Verxina. An overall body-size parameter could cover this.
kept.quote: 3歳時までは馬体重410kg台での出走が殆どであり、キャリア中の最高値でも440kgと小柄な馬体であった。 / まだまだ体は小さいし、じっくりと育てたい
kept.note: All quotes are confirmed. ja.wikipedia calls her the lightest Shuka Sho winner in history (同レース優勝馬史上最少馬体重). netkeiba quotes Tomomichi. uma-furusato (Northern Farm staff) has 「ヴィルシーナを小柄にしたような印象」.

kept.description: A big-striding horse. After his debut win, Christophe Lemaire said 'his stride is big' [跳びが大きくて]. Trainer Katsuhiko Sumii called him supple and springy and said his big stride was a strength [跳びが大きいのがいい].
kept.quote: ルメールは「跳びが大きくて、直線を向いて反応が良かった。…」 … 「柔らかくてバネがある。跳びが大きいのがいい」と話した。
kept.note: Both quotes are in Sponichi's 2016-12-12 Hanshin debut report. Two experts said 跳びが大きい, so 1.07 is fair.

kept.description: Trainer Yasuyuki Tsujino said Kiseki raises his head a little when ridden hard, and that he had always done so.
kept.quote: He has always run calmly and he does raise his head a bit when he’s pushed, but he has always done that.
kept.note: The quote is in Tsujino's 2021 Arima Kinen comments, as part of a description of workouts. It says 'a bit' and only 'when pushed', but it is a lifelong habit. A mild 0.3 is acceptable; 0.2 would also be defensible.

kept.description: Her hind-leg drive was exceptional. Her farrier, Hironobu Ushimaru, said the hindquarters' kick was beyond other horses [蹴る力が他馬と比べものにならない]. She stepped under herself so deeply that her hind feet struck and injured her front feet (overreaching, 「追突」). She wore special protective shoes from age 3 until she went back to normal shoes at the 2019 Arima Kinen, aged 4.
kept.quote: 圧倒的なパフォーマンスを生み出しているのは、トモ（後肢）の推進力。「蹴る力が他馬と比べものにならない。激しい時は、後ろ脚がドーンといっちゃう」 / 「後ろ脚の蹴りが強過ぎて前脚と交錯。俗にいう“追突”というヤツで爪を痛めてしまったため」
kept.note: The Hochi quote is from farrier 牛丸広伸, and the Number quote is from trainer Kunieda. ja.wikipedia has a whole section ('追突') on the strength of her hind legs. Sponichi (Dec 2019) says she returned to normal shoes at the Arima Kinen. With this much evidence, the maximum value of 1.2 is justified. I changed 'trainer's team' to name the farrier and the trainer.

kept.description: Sponichi's conformation column said her chest depth was unusual for a filly [胸の深さは牝馬離れ]. It called it a big chest that holds large lungs and heart.
kept.quote: 胸の深さは牝馬離れしています。オークス時に指摘した通り、大きな肺や心臓を収容する大きな胸です。
kept.note: The quote is in Sponichi's 2018 Shuka Sho conformation column, whose headline is 牝馬離れした胸の深さ. The column also says she was assessed the same way before the Oaks. 1.1 is fair.

kept.description: A big, powerful stride. Lemaire named her big stride as her strong point [跳びが大きい] and said she accelerates with her long legs. He also said 'her strides kept getting bigger' and spoke of 'her powerful strides'. Number described her passing horses with big strides [大きなストライド].
kept.quote: （ストロングポイントは）跳びが大きいですね。最後は長い脚で加速を上げていって、とても速いです。 / Her strides kept getting bigger and all I had to do was to keep her straight.
kept.note: All four sources contain the cited wording: the Hochi Oka Sho comments, the JRA Oka Sho report, Number page 2 (大きなストライドで), and the 2020 Victoria Mile report ('powerful strides'). 1.08 is fair.

kept.description: Her farrier said she ran with a straight, clean action [真っすぐきれいなフォーム], so her shoes wore down less than other horses'. ja.wikipedia says this came from correcting her left-right balance with shoeing.
kept.quote: アーモンドアイは真っすぐきれいなフォームで走るため、他の馬と比べて蹄鉄の減りも少ない点に驚かされるという。
kept.note: The quote is in Hochi (2020 Tenno Sho Autumn, farrier Ushimaru). A ja.wikipedia footnote repeats 「真っすぐきれいなフォーム」. The source is about straight limb flight more than body sway, but 0.7 is still a fair, moderate reading.

kept.description: A distinctive foreleg action. Using a wide range of joint movement, she seemed to fling her forelegs out from the shoulder [肩から前肢を投げ出すような独特の走法]. A foreleg-reach/extension parameter could cover this; it is not the same as high knee action.
kept.quote: 関節の広い可動域を生かして、肩から前肢を投げ出すような独特の走法も変わらない。
kept.note: The quote is in Sponichi's 2020 Japan Cup final-work report. The writer calls it 独特 (distinctive). No parameter fits, so it stays null.

kept.description: Her right foreleg was longer than her left [左前肢より長い右前肢], and her overreaching hind feet hit that longer right fore. ja.wikipedia adds that her right front was shod 6 mm higher to balance the two sides. This is a limb-length asymmetry that no current parameter covers.
kept.quote: 踏み込んだ後肢は長い方の前肢にぶつかる。左前肢より長い右前肢の蹄には3歳春から保護材を着用していたが
kept.note: The quote is in Sponichi (Dec 2019, farrier Ushimaru). A ja.wikipedia footnote backs it up: 「右前脚を左前脚よりも6ミリメートル…高く設定し、左右差のバランスを保たせようとしていた」. No parameter fits, so it stays null.

kept.description: He had a big head. Trainer Masahiro Otake said the horse raced in a shadow roll not to correct his behaviour but to look better, 'because he is a big-faced horse' [顔の大きな馬 / 巨漢で顔が大きい馬].
kept.quote: 「顔の大きな馬なので見栄えを良くするようにシャドーロールを着けて」（大竹）
kept.note: The quote is on Number page 2 and is attributed to Otake. ja.wikipedia's tack section says 「巨漢で顔が大きい馬なので、見栄えを良くするため」. Part of the big face may come from his large overall frame. But a shadow roll used to change how the face looks suggests it looked big in proportion, so 1.12 stands.

kept.description: An unusually large, heavy colt, raced at 520-550 kg and described as a 巨漢 and a 大型馬. An overall body-size parameter could cover this.
kept.quote: He is an unusually large Thoroughbred who has weighed between 520 kg and 550 kg for his track appearances. / 「大型馬で、まだ背中や腰に緩さを残していた」
kept.note: Both quotes are confirmed. The Sportiva quote is from Kimiya of Northern Farm Tenei. ja.wikipedia uses 巨漢. No parameter fits, so it stays null.

kept.description: His legs turned inward (toed-in) from birth [生まれた時から脚が内向していて], so the farm brought him on carefully. A limb-alignment parameter could cover this.
kept.quote: 中島文彦場長（５０）は「生まれた時から脚が内向していて、苦労した馬でした。体が立派な分、内向が不安だったけど、スタッフのおかげですね」
kept.note: The quote is in Daily Sports' 2018 Arima Kinen article, from Northern Farm manager Nakajima. ja.wikipedia: 「出生時より脚が内向しており、慎重に育成が進められた」. No parameter fits, so it stays null.

kept.description: An unusually large mare, weighing up to 524 kg during her career. An overall body-size parameter could cover this.
kept.quote: She is an unusually large female Thoroughbred, weighing as much as 524 kg during her racing career.
kept.note: The quote is on English Wikipedia. The ja.wikipedia race record confirms 524 kg in the 2020 Takarazuka Kinen and Sapporo Kinen, with about 520 kg in her other 2020 races. 'Unusually large' is English Wikipedia's own description, but the weights support it. No parameter fits, so it stays null.

kept.description: Slim, fine frame. Suzuki's 2020 body analysis (Takarazuka Kinen, age 4) says her frame was slim by nature [骨格はスリム] even after she filled out. He says she carried supple, fine muscle suited to middle distances, unlike her heavily muscled miler half-sister Normcore. In a December 2018 interview the interviewer called her 'slender-type' [スレンダー型] from her body. Trainer Saito agreed, adding that at 430-440 kg she was about standard size for a filly.
kept.quote: 元々、骨格はスリムでも蝶のようにバランスが取れた馬体。…筋肉マッチョなマイラー体形の半姉ノームコア…とは対照的なしなやかで繊細な筋肉を身につけた中距離体形。(Sponichi 2020)；－：馬体だけを見ると、スレンダー型ですね。斉：そうですね。430～40キロくらいですけど、背が極端に低い訳でもないですし (keibalab 2018)
kept.note: The Sponichi quote is verified word for word. On keibalab (live site refused the connection, so I read the Wayback copy) the interviewer says スレンダー型, not trainer Saito, who only agreed ('そうですね') and said she was standard-sized for a filly ('サイズは標準くらい'). I fixed the attribution in the description. bone 0.95 stays as a mild reading of 骨格はスリム.

kept.description: Pitch-type runner. A stride-pitch blog analysis (Mahmoud, note.com, June 2021) covered all 15 of her races. It compared her 2020 Takarazuka Kinen, 2020 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 2021 Takarazuka Kinen with four foreign horses, including the English Oaks winners Love and Snowfall. It concluded that her running is far more pitch-type [断然ピッチタイプ]. The source is an amateur data blog, not an official one.
kept.quote: 今回の記事では外国馬都合4頭の完歩ピッチを紹介した形になりましたが、クロノジェネシスの方が断然ピッチタイプの走りの質と言えます。
kept.note: The quote is on the page, which is about the real horse (dated 2021-06-30, written for her Arc run). The comparison is only with four foreign horses (Love, Snowfall and others), not with Thoroughbreds in general, so the mild 0.95 is the right strength. The source is a blog, so confidence stays low.

kept.description: Colt-like, robust body with a big, full belly [立派な腹袋 / 腹袋はたくましい]. Suzuki says it repeatedly ('just like a colt'). In June 2021 he said she looked round enough to seem almost heavy.
kept.quote: 張りに満ちたトモと肩、立派な腹袋。…相変わらず牡馬のようなたくましさです。(2021)；肩が筋肉で厚みを増し、腹袋はたくましい。(2020)
kept.note: Both quotes are in the Sponichi 達眼 articles about this horse (Tenno Sho Spring 2021, Japan Cup 2020). 1.06 is a moderate reading of 腹袋. That term partly reflects condition and appetite, not ribcage shape alone, so I would not push it higher.

kept.description: Well-muscled, colt-like hindquarters [張りに満ちたトモ]. The headline credits her quarters, shoulders and belly with 'colt-like toughness'.
kept.quote: トモ、肩、腹袋から感じる牡馬のようなたくましさ／張りに満ちたトモと肩
kept.note: The headline and body text match. The 1.05 value is modest and fair.

kept.description: Slightly short-coupled (compact-bodied) middle-distance build [少し詰まり気味の中距離体形]. No parameter for body length exists, so this is a candidate for a new one.
kept.quote: 少し詰まり気味の中距離体形。
kept.note: The exact sentence is in the June 2021 Takarazuka Kinen 達眼 article about her. In April 2021 Suzuki also said 'ステイヤー体形ではありません', which is consistent.

kept.description: As a 3-year-old (2019 Oaks) she stood with her tail raised when tense [尾を上げてキンキン]. The habit faded by four, and it describes her standing, not racing.
kept.quote: 3歳時は尾を上げてキンキンしていましたが、4歳秋を迎えて力みが取れ、ゆったりと立っています。(2020)；一昨年のオークス（2着）時は尾を上げてキンキンしていましたが、歳月は馬の気性も成長させる。(2021)
kept.note: Both articles say it. It was temporary and a standing behaviour, so leaving param null is correct and it should not map to run.tailCarriage.

kept.description: Massive, thick quarters that would shame a colt [牡馬顔負けの分厚いトモ], with rock-like muscle in the shoulders and quarters. Suzuki says she grew from a miler into a sprinter-type build as she aged.
kept.quote: 桜花賞時も牡馬顔負けの分厚いトモでしたが、わずか1カ月足らずでさらに筋肉量を増やして段違いにパワーアップしている。(2019)；太い首、肩とトモには岩のような大きな筋肉。(2021)；加齢とともに筋肉量が増えてマイラー体形からスプリンター体形に変わりました。(2021.5)
kept.note: All three quotes are present in Sponichi 達眼 articles about her. Her weight rose from 476 to over 500 kg, which Suzuki attributes to muscle. 1.12 is high but fits repeated, emphatic wording.

kept.description: Thick, powerful neck [太い首 / 立派な首].
kept.quote: 太い首、肩とトモには岩のような大きな筋肉。(2021)；分厚い胸、立派な首、大きな腹袋…。全てが野太い。(2019)
kept.note: Both quotes are present. 1.25 sits within the vocabulary's thick-crest range.

kept.description: Thick, deep breast [分厚い胸].
kept.quote: 分厚い胸、立派な首、大きな腹袋…。
kept.note: The quote is present. 分厚い胸 is ambiguous between breadth and depth. A mild chestWidth value is a fair reading.

kept.description: Forelegs slightly short, so her balance tips a little forward [前脚がやや短いため、重心がやや前傾]. The same column describes a sloping croup [斜尻] and deeply angled, sickle-type hocks [曲飛]. It comes from a single body-analysis column by an ex-farm staffer. No leg-length parameter exists, so it is a candidate for a new one.
kept.quote: 前脚がやや短いため、重心がやや前傾。
kept.note: The live keibalab site refused the connection, so I read the Wayback snapshot (2019 NHK Mile Cup 馬体FOCUS). The sentence is in the block for the 4-race, 3-win Oka Sho / Saudi Arabia RC winner, which is Gran Alegria. Only one source, so confidence stays low.

kept.description: Runs with her neck carried somewhat upright, more 'up' than her full brother Real Steel, who stretched out [首を立てて走る / 起きて走っている]. Her trainer Yahagi confirmed this.
kept.quote: －：走法的に言えば、リアルスティールはちょっと伸びて走る感じがあったのですが、この馬はちょっと首を立てて走りますね。矢：たしかにリアルスティールより起きて走っていますね。
kept.note: The live site refused the connection, so I read the Wayback copy of the May 2019 Yahagi interview before the Oaks. The interviewer makes the observation and Yahagi agrees, as the description says. 'ちょっと' (slightly) justifies the small 0.3.

kept.description: Yahagi says that when she lowers her neck she first sinks and then stretches out [首を下げる時に沈んでから伸ばす走法], which reads as a pronounced dip-and-reach neck action.
kept.quote: 首を下げる時に沈んでから伸ばす走法ですね。間違いなくそういうところがありますよね。
kept.note: The quote is present, spoken by Yahagi. The wording is loose ('沈んで' could also mean the body dipping), but a neck that is held up and then dropped and stretched implies a larger neck amplitude, so a moderate neckPump of 1.15 is a fair reading. Do not raise it.

kept.description: Upright front pasterns [両前のつなぎは立ち気味]. The right fore hoof, also described as upright, wore a glue-on Equilox shoe (2019 Elizabeth Queen Cup, 2020 Arima Kinen). This is a candidate for a pastern or hoof-angle parameter.
kept.quote: 両前のつなぎは立ち気味ですが、昨年のエリザベス女王杯時に着けていた右前のエクイロックス（接着装蹄）は外してきた。(2020.5)；立ち気味の右前蹄にエクイロックスを施しています。(2020.12)
kept.note: Both quotes are present in Sponichi 達眼 pieces about her. The shoe was off in May 2020 and back on in December 2020.

kept.description: Habitually stands with both hind legs stretched out behind her [両トモを流した立ち方]. This is a standing posture, not a running one.
kept.quote: 両トモを流した立ち方は相変わらずですが
kept.note: The quote is present, and '相変わらず' supports calling it a habit. It describes standing only.

kept.description: High-set tail [尾の付け根が上に付いている]. Suzuki notes that quarters usually look plain on horses with a high-set tail, but hers still look impressive because of the muscle.
kept.quote: 尾の付け根が上に付いている馬はトモが見栄えしづらいもの。それでも格好良く映るのは筋肉が質量ともに際立っているからです。
kept.note: The quote is present in the 2020 Oka Sho 達眼 article on her. The tail set is stated by implication, but clearly about her. 0.5 is fair.

kept.description: Her standout feature is muscular, bulging hindquarters [特長はトモ / 筋肉で隆起したトモ]. Her quarters were still strong in 2022.
kept.quote: 英語で「大胆な戦法」（デアリングタクト）と命名された青鹿毛の特長はトモにあります。／筋肉で隆起したトモがあれば大胆な戦法も取れます。(2020)；特に肩とトモの筋肉は3冠当時と比べても見劣りしません。(2022)
kept.note: Both quotes are present (the 2022 Elizabeth Queen Cup piece is a reprint of Sponichi's column on netkeiba). 1.1 is fair.

kept.description: In one 2020 photo her ears were spread outward in a 'ハ' shape [ハの字に広げた耳]. Suzuki reads this, with her sharp eyes and pointed muzzle, as an expression of her fierce temper, not as conformation. It is kept as an expression note and does not set static ear placement.
kept.quote: 顔立ちは非常にきつい。鋭い目、とがらせた鼻、ハの字に広げた耳。激しい気性がうかがえます。
kept.note: The quote is present, but the context is facial expression and temperament ('激しい気性がうかがえます') in a single photo, not ear conformation. Mapping it to static conf.earSet 0.4 overreads it, so I changed param to null. It could feed a future ear-expression or temperament parameter.

kept.description: Big, dynamic, long-striding action [完歩の大きいダイナミックなフットワーク]. Suzuki credits his clean neck-set and sloping shoulder for it. His trainer Shikato repeatedly called him a horse with a big action [フットワークが大きい].
kept.quote: きれいに抜けた首差しと滑らかに傾斜した肩（肩甲骨）が完歩の大きいダイナミックなフットワークを生み出します。(Sponichi)；フットワークが大きい方ですし、やはり中山コースよりは東京コースの方が向いていると思います。(鹿戸, netkeiba)；フットワークの大きい馬なので1600mでも短いくらいかなと思っていました。(鹿戸, Wikipedia)
kept.note: All three sources contain the quoted statements about this horse. 1.07 is fair for consistent 'big action' comments.

kept.description: Strong hocks, angled well with the quarters, that turn their power straight into forward drive [強固な飛節がトモのパワーを逃さず推進力に変えています].
kept.quote: 車のエンジン部にあたるトモ（後肢）と絶妙な角度でリンクした強固な飛節がトモのパワーを逃さず推進力に変えています。
kept.note: The quote is present (also cited in ja.wikipedia's 身体的特徴 section). It is a conformation-based inference about drive, so the modest 1.08 is appropriate.

kept.description: Long-legged and long-bodied [脚長で胴伸びの良い馬体], per the Carrot Club yearling catalog quoted in Wikipedia. This is a candidate for leg-length and body-length parameters.
kept.quote: 母父の影響を色濃く反映した脚長で胴伸びの良い馬体は、父の産駒傾向とは若干趣を異にしていますが
kept.note: The quote is present in ja.wikipedia, which also gives yearling figures nearby (体高158.0cm, 胸囲176.5cm, 管囲20.8cm). It is a sales-catalog description, so confidence should stay moderate.

kept.description: Voluminous breast muscle [胸前の筋肉はボリューム満点]. Suzuki also noted raised, prominent shoulder and breast muscle in 2021.
kept.quote: 胸前やトモの筋肉はボリューム満点です。(2023)；せり上がった肩と胸前の筋肉。(2021)
kept.note: Both quotes are present (2023 and 2021 Arima Kinen 達眼). 1.06 is fair.

kept.description: Voluminous hindquarter muscle on a typical stayer's frame [典型的なステイヤー体形].
kept.quote: 胸前やトモの筋肉はボリューム満点です。　典型的なステイヤー体形。
kept.note: The quote is present. The value is modest, which suits a stayer's frame.

kept.description: Raised, prominent withers [キ甲が盛り上がり].
kept.quote: キ甲が盛り上がり、ヒ腹も張っていますが、立ち姿がおとなしい。
kept.note: The quote is present. There is a single mention, so 0.4 is a fair moderate value.

kept.description: Breeder Okada says Titleholder had a big, dynamic action in training. In his 2021 classic prep and classic (Yayoi Sho, Satsuki Sho) he ran pitching forward without using his neck, so riders took him for a pitch runner. Okada says he was only immature, and that the long, free-reaching action [伸びやかなフットワーク] returned by the 2022 Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen. The value models his mature style.
kept.quote: 育成中は「肩が出て、飛節も伸びて、ダイナミックなフットワークをしていた」／乗るジョッキーはピッチ走法だと思っちゃう。ピッチ走法じゃなくて幼いだけなんだよね／それが一年を経て、伸びやかなフットワークが戻ってきました。
kept.note: The quotes are in the Pacalla (Okada Stud) piece dated 2022-09-29. 'つんのめって走っている…首も使えなくて' refers to the Yayoi Sho and Satsuki Sho. 1.05 for the mature style is a fair, modest reading.

kept.description: Habitually stood with his forelegs set forward, leaning forward [前肢を前踏み / 前方にせり出すように立っていた]. By autumn 2023 he stood with his weight further back. This is a standing posture, a candidate parameter.
kept.quote: 前肢を前踏みした見栄えのしない姿勢ですが、実にタフな馬です。(2021)；以前は前方にせり出すように立っていたのに今秋は後方に重心を置いています。(2023)
kept.note: Both quotes are present. It is a standing habit that changed by 2023, so param stays null.

kept.description: Big horse with a big, long-reaching stride [大型馬で跳びも大きい]. In August 2026 his team chose the widest-cornered course at Hakodate for his work because of his big action [フットワークの大きい走り].
kept.quote: 大型馬で跳びも大きいため、三つのなかで最もコーナーの広い芝コースを選択。／大きな馬体を大きく使って徐々にスピードに乗ると (Sanspo)；フットワークの大きい走りに適したコースを探った結果 (Tospo headline)
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/フォーエバーヤング_(競走馬)
kept.note: The Sanspo text is verified word for word, the Tospo headline says the same, and ja.wikipedia restates it ('大型馬で、しかも跳びも大きいというのが特徴'). 1.08 is fair.

kept.description: Exceptionally thick neck. His regular jockey Ryusei Sakai posted that the height of his eye-line, the thickness of his neck [首の太さ] and his stability at top speed are completely different from other horses.
kept.quote: ちなみに目線の高さや首の太さ、トップスピードでの安定感は他の馬と全然違います
kept.note: Sanspo quotes Sakai's X post word for word. 'Completely different from other horses' supports a clearly above-average 1.3. It is still a single jockey remark, not a body-analysis piece.

kept.description: Massive overall frame, described as imposing [馬体は雄大そのもの]. A stable assistant said he weighed about 580 kg unsaddled in January 2026, with a planned race weight of about 560 kg; he raced at 526 kg on debut and 543 kg at the end of 2024. No overall size or scale parameter exists, so this is a candidate for one.
kept.quote: 馬体は雄大そのもので「今は裸で580キロぐらい。これからの調教や飛行機での輸送もあるのでレースでは560キロ前後で出走させたい」
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/フォーエバーヤング_(競走馬)
kept.note: The quote is verified (Sponichi, 2026-01-10, assistant 渋田). The original 'about 570-580 kg' did not match the source, which gives about 580 kg unsaddled and a race weight of about 560 kg. I corrected the figures and added the race weights from the ja.wikipedia record (526 kg debut, 543 kg in the 2024 Tokyo Daishoten).
